adjoe builds the technologies behind mobile apps growth and monetization. adjoe Ads is our programmatic in-app advertising platform that seamlessly connects advertisers and publishers through direct integration of our Android and iOS SDKs. Every ad decision happens in under 200ms across 10 million daily users, powered by real-time bidding algorithms and user quality prediction models that match the right ad to the right user at the right moment.
 Engine Behind 120M Processed Auctions Daily
 The Ad Network team builds and operates the backend services that power adjoe Ads' programmatic advertising engine. The core challenge is straightforward to state and hard to solve: for every incoming ad request from a mobile SDK, decide within milliseconds whether it's a good fit for any active campaign — and at what price to bid.
To solve this, the team has built a Real-Time Bidding platform of 20+ Go microservices that orchestrate ad auctions at 1,500 bid requests per second , integrate with external demand partners via OpenRTB , and connect to ML models making 50 billion predictions daily across 600+ features to optimize bid pricing. The stack runs on Kubernetes , with Kafka handling event streaming, DynamoDB and Elasticache powering low-latency data access, and Prometheus and Grafana providing observability across the entire system.
 Your Mission & Who We Are Looking For: 
 Golang Backend Foundation: You have a Computer Science degree (or related field) and hands-on experience writing Golang. You will use this foundation to contribute directly to our production backend services from day one at adjoe, rather than writing isolated or throwaway code.
 Proven Project Portfolio: We look for engineers with tangible projects to show, not just coursework. You will leverage the architectural lessons from your past builds—what worked, why you built it, and what you would change—to design and scale our live systems.
 Modern Infrastructure Stack: You are comfortable working with REST APIs, version control via Git, and CI/CD pipelines. You will use these core tools, along with your familiarity in cloud platforms like AWS, GCP, or Azure, to reliably deploy your code into our environments.
 Iterative Code Ownership: You will work alongside experienced engineers who will rigorously review your pull requests. We need someone who parses technical feedback directly and uses it to continuously refine their system design and coding standards.
 🌎 We welcome applications from talent worldwide and provide relocation support to Hamburg, Germany for those ready to join our team. 
 What’s in It for You? 
 At adjoe, you’re not here to just close JIRA tickets, you’re helping build the infrastructure behind one of the most impactful platforms in adtech. The systems you work on will reach hundreds of millions of users and power billions of decisions every day.
 Go Big. Own projects with impact on 770M users and push adtech boundaries.
 Move Fast. Ship solutions multiple times a day, learn from results, and keep momentum.
 Be Direct. Solve problems openly and collaborate across teams.
 Thrive Together. Grow with a diverse, global team of people from over 40 different countries that learn from each other.
 Have Fun. Celebrate wins, enjoy daily victories, and bring your energy.
 Our mission is to create an inspiring work environment for amazing people to achieve extraordinary things. Be part of it !
 Skip writing cover letters. Tell us about your most passionate personal project, your desired salary, and your earliest possible start date. We are looking forward to your application!
 We welcome applications from people who will contribute to the diversity of our company.

Who We Are
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards.
As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously.
We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications.
 The role
 Helsing builds software and AI that makes existing defence hardware up to ten times more capable. The sensing stack is where that capability begins. Without precise, synchronised, calibrated sensor data, the AI has nothing to work with.
As Multimodal Sensing and Fusion Engineer, you will own that stack end to end. You will architect the multimodal perception front-end that combines electro-optical and long-wave infrared cameras, radar, LiDAR, and inertial sensing into a single, coherent input to Helsing's AI. You will translate mission requirements into concrete specifications for sensor selection, placement, synchronisation, and calibration, and you will define the safety concepts that ensure the system degrades gracefully and fails safe in the field.
This is not a prototyping role. The systems you design go into operational environments. The quality of the data you deliver directly affects the decisions Helsing's AI supports in the field. You will sit at the intersection of hardware engineers, electrical engineers, and AI and computer-vision researchers, working out of Munich, Berlin or London.
The day-to-day
 Define the multimodal sensing architecture: select and integrate EO and LWIR cameras, radar, LiDAR, and IMUs, aligning requirements with the AI team to optimise algorithm performance and balance trade-offs across size, weight, power, cost, and robustness. 
 Own sensor synchronisation: design and implement time synchronisation across heterogeneous sensors using PTP/gPTP, PPS, and hardware triggers such as Hsync and Vsync, so all modalities share a common, precise time base. 
 Own sensor calibration: develop intrinsic, extrinsic, spatial, and temporal calibration procedures, including online and continuous recalibration, across cameras, radar, and IMU. 
 Define safety concepts: derive failure modes, fault detection, isolation, and recovery concepts for the sensing subsystem, drawing on both defence mission-safety thinking and automotive functional-safety practice (ISO 26262, SOTIF). 
 Drive system design and architecture: analyse the interplay of hardware, software, and algorithm architectures, and define the interfaces and data pipelines from sensor to AI. 
 Bring hardware to life: spend hands-on time in the lab bringing up prototypes, testing performance under varying conditions, and supporting integration into the software stack. 
 Tune data quality: analyse application-specific sensing performance and adjust designs and low-level algorithms to maximise the value sensor data provides to downstream AI applications.

 A Ph.D. or M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 
 A professional track record building multimodal sensing or sensor-fusion systems combining at least two of: cameras (EO and/or LWIR), radar, LiDAR, and IMU. 
 Demonstrated understanding of system-level synchronisation, including PTP/gPTP, PPS, and hardware triggers such as Hsync and Vsync. 
 Mastery of sensor calibration, intrinsic and extrinsic, spatial and temporal, including strategies for maintaining calibration across a multi-sensor rig over its operational lifetime. 
 The ability to derive safety concepts for a sensing or perception subsystem, from a defence or mission-critical background, an automotive functional-safety background (ISO 26262, SOTIF), or both. 
 Strong systems design instincts, comfortable reasoning about the interplay of hardware, software, and algorithms. 
 Proficiency in C/C++ or Rust for low-level firmware development and hardware-software interface debugging, plus Python. 
 Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.

 Depth in one or more of the following sensor modalities: thermal imaging (LWIR design, calibration, and programming), FMCW radar signal processing (detection, clustering, and tracking), or LiDAR and point-cloud processing including cross-calibration with cameras and radar. 
 IMU and inertial navigation expertise, including GNSS/INS integration, bias and error modelling, and sensor alignment.

 A background in automotive, robotics, or aerospace sensor fusion, covering ADAS, AUTOSAR, ROS, or ISO 26262 and SOTIF, and familiarity with how sensor data feeds downstream computer-vision or AI pipelines. 
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields

The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve.  In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts

About us
 We are building a global leader in physical AI, anchored in Europe’s strongest robotics heritage. Founded by entrepreneurs with backgrounds in scaling digital products and advanced robotics, the team is bolstered by senior leadership from top-tier AI research labs and industrial tech companies.
 Driven by a mission to create versatile and trustworthy embodied AI for physical labor, we fuse deep engineering mastery in AI and mechatronics with a rapid-execution culture. We are addressing the labor shortage by closing the gap to production-grade deployment. This means building the trusted alternative: robots that are safe, secure, and engineered to automotive standards of scale and durability.
 We are well-capitalized and now assembling our team.
 Our Locations: Vesoma has two main locations: Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus. This pan-European setup represents our core ambition of building a European technology leader, gives us a great talent base and a strong corporate structure.
 Your mission 
 The role
 As an AI Research Engineer, you enter as a key member of the early AI team. You will work directly with our AI leadership to define the research direction for how our humanoid robots learn. You research self-learning systems for robot foundation models, turn ideas into working prototypes and push the state of the art - measured not by how good a result looks in a paper, but by how well it holds up against strong baselines and, ultimately, on real hardware. You build on our large-scale training, RL post-training and simulation infrastructure, and your research needs shape where it goes next. This is a full-time, permanent position.
 Your profile 
 Key responsibilities 
 Research on Self-Learning Systems: Develop methods that let our robot foundation models learn from large-scale video and robot data and keep improving from experience - across pre-training, imitation learning and RL post-training - for humanoid locomotion and manipulation
 Prototyping: Turn research ideas and new papers into working prototypes quickly, in simulation and on physical robots.
 Pushing the State of the Art: Track the frontier of robot learning and foundation models, identify what matters for real-world deployment, and develop methods that move beyond it
 Experimentation: Design and run experiments at scale on our GPU fleet - from simulation to hardware - with clean setups that produce results the team can trust.
 Evaluation: Benchmark rigorously against strong baselines using our simulation benchmarks and real-world tests, run ablations and make results reproducible, so decisions rest on evidence rather than impressions.
 Sim-to-Real Collaboration: Work with the simulation, hardware and controls teams so that what is learned in simulation transfers to the robot.
 Who we are looking for
 We seek people who embrace the empirical nature of AI research and are ready to move beyond demos to real-world deployment.
 Experience: 3+ years of research experience in machine learning or robotics, ideally with a track record in robot learning or large-scale models. [A PhD in a related field is a plus.] [Publications at top venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, NeurIPS or ICML are a plus.]
 Core Skills: Deep knowledge of learning-based methods for robotics and strong engineering skills to implement them. In detail:
 Learning Methods: Hands-on research experience with robot foundation models or policy learning - e.g. VLAs, diffusion/flow-matching policies, imitation learning or RL post-training.
 Engineering: Strong Python and PyTorch and/or JAX; able to write research code that others can build on.
 Simulation: Experience with physics simulators for robot learning (MuJoCo/MjLab, Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim or comparable).
 Experimental Rigor: Experience designing experiments, choosing meaningful baselines and evaluating results honestly.
 A plus: Deploying learned policies on real robots; training large models on multi-node GPU clusters; multimodal or video models.
 Mindset: You balance the agility of a startup with the professional rigor required for a global industrial player. You are a curious builder who thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced research environment - and you care whether a method works on the robot, not just on the benchmark.
 Why us?
 The Team : Work alongside leadership with a proven track record of building unicorn-scale companies and defining global robotics standards.
 Smart Strategy : We operate as disciplined fast followers. Capital is timed to the deployment inflection point, avoiding early-mover dead ends to scale fast on proven foundations.
 Resources : We are substantially internally funded and attract top-tier investors to avoid any capital constraints for our mission.
 Historic Opportunity : Join at the dawn of a new industry comparable to the rise of the automobile. Help shape the European champion in this trillion-dollar market.
 We are an equal opportunity employer.

We Are Sparta 
Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.
Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.
We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.
At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.
Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.
 The role
 You lead how Sparta builds software in the AI era. You own our AI-native software development lifecycle: the development agents engineers work alongside, the CI/CD that ships their code, and the testing strategy that lets us move fast without breaking trading workflows.
 AI has changed how code gets written, reviewed, and tested, and the tooling has not caught up. Your job is to make an engineer with Claude Code, a good harness and a fast pipeline several times more effective, and to prove it with data, not anecdotes.
 What you will do
 Own the AI development toolchain. Set up and evolve Claude Code and other development agents across engineering: shared skills, MCP servers, repo context, and guardrails, so agents work well in our codebase out of the box.
 Build agents into the lifecycle. Automate the work around the code: AI-assisted code review, test generation, dependency upgrades, migrations and incident triage, with humans in the loop where it matters.
 Make CI/CD fast and boring. Own build, test and release pipelines across the Nx monorepo: caching, affected-only builds, preview environments and safe, frequent deploys to AWS.
 Build the guardrails for everyone who builds. Anyone can build now, including product, design, data and domain experts working with agents. Create the tooling that makes it safe for them to contribute code: automated quality gates, code ownership and review rules, preview environments, policy checks and agent evals in the pipeline, so good changes ship fast and risky ones are caught early. Testing strategy sits inside this: define what we test at each level and make the right tests cheap to write.
 Keep it secure. Secrets, permissions and sandboxing for agents that read code and run commands, and supply-chain checks in the pipeline.
 Raise the bar for everyone. Run enablement, write the playbooks, pair with teams and turn good practice from one team into the default for all of engineering.
 What you bring
 Extensive experience as a hands-on software engineer, with recent focus on developer experience, platform or build and release engineering.
 You have rolled out AI coding tools to a team and made them stick: you know where agents help, where they fail and how to set them up for a real codebase.
 You lead without needing authority: you treat engineers as customers, listen first, and win adoption with tools people want to use.
 Nice to have
 Built Claude Code skills, plugins or MCP servers, or extended another agent harness.
 Deep CI/CD experience: you have designed pipelines for a monorepo, cut build and test times, and run safe, frequent releases.
 Infrastructure as code and container platforms.
 Experience defining or running engineering metrics.
 Our stack for this team
 Claude Ecosystem · Nx monorepo · GitHub · AWS · TypeScript · Python · Kotlin
 Why Join Sparta?
 At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.
 • Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company
 • $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment
 • Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale
 • Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence
 • Top-tier tools and technology to support your success
 What's the Culture Like at Sparta?
 At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.
 The Sparta Code
 Understanding is non-negotiable 
 Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. 
 The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.
 Ask for forgiveness, not for permission 
 Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not. 
 90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.
 Fall in love with the problem 
 The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to. 
 Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.
 It's your fault. Lucky you. 
 If it's on you, it's in your control. 
 True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.
 Conflict is a gift 
 Honesty is an expression of care. 
 Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

 At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.
 The Sparta Code
 Understanding is non-negotiable 
 Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. 
 The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.
 Ask for forgiveness, not for permission 
 Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not. 
 90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.
 Fall in love with the problem 
 The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to. 
 Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.
 It's your fault. Lucky you. 
 If it's on you, it's in your control. 
 True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.
 Conflict is a gift 
 Honesty is an expression of care. 
 Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

We Are 
 Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 
 You Are 
 You are someone who gets a quiet satisfaction from finding the bug no one else caught, from writing a script that saves the team three hours a week, from seeing a pattern in test data that points to something fixable. You do not just run tests, you think about what they mean and what they are missing. You know that quality is not something you inspect in at the end, it is something you build into the process from the start. 
 Scripting is not a chore for you. Whether it is Python or Tcl, you see automation as a way to make repetitive work disappear so you can focus on the problems that actually need a human. You are comfortable sitting with a dataset, pulling it apart, and surfacing the insight that changes how the team approaches the next release cycle. 
 You are early in your career but already understand that good engineering is about details, follow-through, and clear communication. You ask questions when something does not make sense. You document what you learn. You show up ready to contribute, not just observe.  At Synopsys, you will work on Embedded Memory IP that powers the devices people use every day, and the quality work you do here will matter. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Coordinate kickoff and release meetings with cross-functional teams to ensure compliance and process alignment throughout development and verification.
 Run regression test suites on Embedded Memory IP releases and track results across validation cycles.
 Analyze test data to surface trends, flag anomalies, and identify root causes of failures or quality gaps.
 Write and maintain Python and Tcl automation scripts that streamline testing, reporting, and compliance workflows.
 Document test outcomes, process gaps, and improvement recommendations in clear, actionable formats.
 Support the team in refining Quality Management System processes based on real-world validation feedback.
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Deliver zero-defect Embedded Memory IP to customers by catching issues before they reach production.
 Enable faster, more reliable releases through automation that reduces manual testing overhead.
 Surface data-driven insights that help engineering teams make better decisions about where to focus next.
 Strengthen the Quality Management System so every release cycle is more efficient than the last.
 Support the development of IP on advanced technology nodes that power AI, mobile, and smart device applications.
 Build a foundation of quality practices that scale as the product portfolio grows.
 What You'll Need 
 Bachelor's degree in Electronics and Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
 0 to 2 years of experience in validation, testing, quality assurance, or a related engineering role.
 Working knowledge of Python or Tcl for scripting and automation.
 Ability to analyze data, identify patterns, and communicate findings clearly.
 Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail, you notice when something is off and you dig into why.
 Who You Are 
 You can take a messy test log, pull out what matters, and explain it to someone who was not in the room.
 You are comfortable working across teams, coordinating meetings, and making sure people have what they need to stay on track.
 You do not wait to be told what to automate, you see repetitive work and you build a script for it.
 You are adaptable and do not get thrown when priorities shift or requirements change mid-cycle.
 You care about doing things right, not just fast, and you are willing to ask for clarity when the path forward is not obvious.
 The Team You'll Be Part Of 
 You will be part of a highly skilled, dynamic team focused on defining and executing processes and methodology for Quality Management of Embedded Memories. You will work closely with cross-functional teams and are committed to continuous learning and improvement, fostering an environment where creativity and technical excellence thrive. 
 Rewards and Benefits 
 We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process. 
 At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

About Boltz
 Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.
 Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.
 We focus on two things:
 Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.
 Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.
 The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.
 You can read more about our mission, research and product vision in our manifesto .
 About the role
 Our partners trust us with their most valuable secrets: unpublished targets, novel molecules and years of proprietary assay data. Your job is to make sure that trust is well placed, everywhere our platform runs: our own cloud, dedicated single-tenant environments, and partners' own AWS and Google Cloud accounts.
 You will be a founding engineer on our security team, part of the Platform team in Core Engineering, shaping the security program with our CTO, who leads it today. You will work with every engineering team at Boltz, and you will sit across the table from the security leaders of the world's largest pharma companies.
 We want security to be the reason a partner says yes faster, not the reason a deal stalls. This role is ideal for a hands-on engineer who would rather fix a control in code than write a document about it, and who can explain risk clearly to a pharma CISO.
 What you'll do
 Make secure the default: build guardrails into our Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD so every new cluster, environment and partner deployment inherits the right boundaries from day one.
 Protect what matters most: keep partner data isolated across tenants and deployments, protect our model weights, and make sure the agents acting on scientists' behalf can only do what they should.
 Make the secure path the easy path: identity, secrets, service-to-service authentication and supply-chain controls that engineers actually want to use.
 See and stop threats: logging, detection and incident response across AWS and GCP, with exercises that keep us sharp.
 Find weaknesses first: threat-model new features before they ship, run penetration tests, and attack our own agents and APIs before anyone else does.
 Turn trust into an advantage: lead security reviews with partners' security teams, translate their requirements into engineering work early, and run our SOC 2 Type II program and the frameworks partners ask for next (e.g. ISO 27001) with evidence generated by our systems, not by screenshots.
 Secure the company: identity, device management, access reviews and security awareness for a small, highly technical team.
 This role is not a compliance-only (GRC) or SOC analyst role. Most of your time goes into engineering; compliance should be a by-product of controls that actually work.
 About you
 Minimum Requirements
 4+ years of security engineering experience in cloud-native SaaS or infrastructure companies.
 Deep, hands-on cloud security experience on AWS or Google Cloud: IAM and multi-account or multi-project organizations, network security, encryption and key management, audit logging and threat detection.
 Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) and enough hands-on engineering to ship security improvements yourself.
 Application security experience: threat modeling, secure code review, authentication and authorization (SSO, OAuth/OIDC, MFA), web and API vulnerabilities.
 Experience owning a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 program through an external audit, or building the controls one depends on.
 Practical incident response experience.
 Low ego, high ownership, and pragmatic trade-offs between risk and speed; clear with engineers, leadership and partners' security teams alike.
 Preferred Requirements
 Kubernetes and container security (network policy, admission control, workload identity, image signing).
 Security for ML or LLM systems: agent tool access, prompt injection, model and training-data protection.
 Experience as an early or founding security hire at a startup.
 Securing deployments in customer-controlled, multi-cloud or regulated environments.
 Exposure to life-sciences or pharma security and data-protection expectations (e.g. GDPR).
 Offensive security or penetration testing background.
 We know great people don't always tick every box. If this role excites you and you meet most of the minimum requirements, we'd like to hear from you.
 What we offer
 Shape the security program that lets the world's leading pharma companies trust frontier AI with their discovery programs.
 Work alongside one of the most talent-dense teams in the field.
 Significant ownership and independence, with responsibility for driving projects from concept to deployment.
 Highly competitive salary with meaningful equity in a public benefit company.
 Benefits: 
 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
 Annual team offsite trip
 Private healthcare (BUPA), covering pre-existing conditions
 Pension program
 Paid parental leave
 Wellhub gym membership
 Free lunch every day
 Travel expenses
 How we hire
 Initial screen with a member of the Talent team
 Security design and threat-modeling interview
 Onsite in London or virtual onsite with the team
 Offer + Onboarding
 Our commitment
 Boltz is committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the hiring process, tell us and we'll make it work.

items.jobDescription:
Who We Are
 Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.
 What We Offer
 Salary:
€44.000,00 - €60.500,00
Location:
Dresden,DEU
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.
At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.
As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. You'll use digital analytics for troubleshooting and apply basic diagnostic techniques to assess and address technical issues. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Additionally, you'll coordinate and communicate directly with customers to ensure smooth operations and exceptional service.
 Field Service Engineer / Customer Engineer - New College Graduate / Early Career Talent
 Kick-start your engineering career with world class training, hands on technical work, and international experience at Applied Materials - the global leader in semiconductor technology.
This role is ideal for recent graduates or early-career engineers who value precision, discipline, and structured learning, and who are adaptable enough to succeed in very different cultural and operational environments.
 What you’ll do: 
 Hands-On Engineering Work
 Learn to install, maintain, and troubleshoot advanced semiconductor equipment with high-complex machine components

items.jobTitle: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Topological Data Analysis for Deep Learning
items.jobDescription: The Department of Computer Science (Dialogue Systems and Machine Learning) at Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf is seeking a Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) in Topological Data Analysis for Deep Learning Job ID: J000000695 Start date: as soon as possible Limited until: 31.12.2027 Location: Düsseldorf Working hours: full time Job category: science / research / teaching Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-L The Dialogue Systems and Machine Learning group at Heinrich Heine University investigates fundamental questions in human–computer interaction, at the intersection of Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning. Our research focuses on building intelligent dialogue systems that can learn, reason, adapt, and interact effectively with humans in dynamic and uncertain environments. We develop principled methods for dialogue modelling, representation learning, reinforcement learning, knowledge acquisition, and user simulation. Our mission is to advance the foundations of machine intelligence towards dialogue systems that are adaptive, trustworthy, and genuinely useful to people. Main tasks We are looking for a talented and enthusiastic researcher to investigate Topological Data Analysis (TDA) and its applications to deep learning, natural language processing, and representation learning. A particular focus will be on understanding whether topological and geometric properties of neural representations can provide interpretable signatures of learning dynamics and important machine learning phenomena. The successful candidate will develop and apply topological methods, design and conduct computational experiments, and publish research in leading venues. The researcher will be a member of the Dialogue Systems and Machine Learning group, led by Prof. Milica Gašić, and will be jointly advised by Prof. Marcus Zibrowius from the Topology and Geometry group, providing an interdisciplinary research environment spanning mathematics, machine learning, and NLP. Your Profile The candidate should hold a completed scientific university education (M.Sc./M.A./Diploma/Magister) in Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field and should hold or be close to obtaining a PhD in Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field. A strong publication record is desirable. Experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable: topological data analysis machine learning deep learning or natural language processing Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, strong programming skills, and the ability to work collaboratively are essential. The ability to teach in German is desirable. Our Offer We offer a full-time position with a competitive salary (EG 13 TV-L) and 4 SWS of teaching duties in relevant courses. The position provides the opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of topological data analysis, machine learning, and natural language processing, while working across mathematical and computational disciplines. The position is initially fixed-term for one year, with the possibility of extension for a further three years, subject to satisfactory performance. It is a qualification position under the Act on Temporary Scientific Contracts (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz, WissZeitVG), intended to support the employee’s further scientific qualification. The start date is negotiable, with 1 January 2027 or earlier preferred. Benefits: Company pension grant Good transport connection Free parking International work Bonus payments Union rates Payment of capital-forming benefits Heinrich Heine University upholds the principle of "Excellence through Diversity". It has signed the "Diversity Charter" and successfully participated in the Stifterverband's audit "Shaping Diversity". It is certified as a family-friendly university and has set itself the goal of promoting diversity among its staff. Applications from people of all genders are expressly welcome. Applications from women will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equal Opportunities Act. The application of severely disabled persons and persons with equivalent disabilities is also welcome. In order for a severe disability or equality to be taken into account, please provide evidence of this with suitable documents. Masterthesis Investigating Electrolyte Additives for All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
items.jobDescription:
The Fraunhofer Institute for Chemical Technology ICT is one of the oldest and largest institutes within the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft.
With a broad range of expertise in polymer technology, chemical processes, explosives technology and safety research, as well as energy and propulsion systems, we develop application-oriented solutions to address complex technological challenges.
Our research spans lightweight engineering and green chemistry to aerospace applications, safety and defense technologies, as well as recycling and sustainability concepts.
In everything we do, we combine scientific expertise, state-of-the-art infrastructure and a strong focus on practical applications.
 Iron redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are promising candidates for large-scale energy storage, as they rely on abundant and potentially cost-effective materials. However, their electrochemical performance and long-term stability depend strongly on the electrolyte composition.In particular, the kinetics and reversibility of iron redox reactions, the deposition and dissolution of metallic iron, hydrogen evolution and electrolyte stability play a crucial role in battery performance.As part of your Master’s thesis, you will investigate the influence of different electrolyte additives and their concentrations on the electrochemical processes in all-iron redox flow batteries. Through systematic electrochemical experiments and cell testing, you will evaluate how changes in electrolyte composition affect the system's performance and stability. Your work will contribute to a better understanding of the underlying electrochemical mechanisms and help identify promising electrolyte formulations for future energy storage applications.
 Be part of change 
 Conduct electrochemical experiments to investigate the influence of different electrolyte additives and concentrations
 Perform electrochemical measurements and redox flow battery cell tests
 Evaluate and interpret experimental data to assess electrochemical performance
 Investigate the influence of electrolyte composition on iron redox reactions and relevant side reactions
 Review relevant scientific literature
 Document and present your findings in a scientific thesis
 What you contribute 
 Background in electrochemistry, chemistry, chemi-cal engineering, materials science or a related field
 Interest in energy-storage technologies and redox-flow batteries
 Experience or interest in electrochemical techniques (CV, EIS, EQCM, etc)
 Experience with LabView is a plus
 Careful and systematic experimental work
 Ability to analyze and interpret experimental data
 Interest in developing a mechanistic understanding of electrochemical processes
 Independent working style and willingness to work in an interdisciplinary research environment
 What we offer 
 A challenging, attractive, interdisciplinary and international working environment
 An appreciative and supportive working atmosphere
 Opportunities for individual professional development
 Flexible working hours through a flexitime arrangement
 Parking facilities, a cafeteria and a library on campus
 … and much more!
 The weekly working hours are up to 20 hours and can be arranged flexibly by mutual agreement.

 CV

items.jobTitle: Masterthesis Investigating Electrolyte Additives for All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
items.jobDescription:
class="jobdescription"> The Fraunhofer Institute for Chemical Technology ICT is one of the oldest and largest institutes within the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft.
With a broad range of expertise in polymer technology, chemical processes, explosives technology and safety research, as well as energy and propulsion systems, we develop application-oriented solutions to address complex technological challenges.
Our research spans lightweight engineering and green chemistry to aerospace applications, safety and defense technologies, as well as recycling and sustainability concepts.
In everything we do, we combine scientific expertise, state-of-the-art infrastructure and a strong focus on practical applications.
 Iron redox flow batteries (IRFBs) are promising candidates for large-scale energy storage, as they rely on abundant and potentially cost-effective materials. However, their electrochemical performance and long-term stability depend strongly on the electrolyte composition.In particular, the kinetics and reversibility of iron redox reactions, the deposition and dissolution of metallic iron, hydrogen evolution and electrolyte stability play a crucial role in battery performance.As part of your Master’s thesis, you will investigate the influence of different electrolyte additives and their concentrations on the electrochemical processes in all-iron redox flow batteries. Through systematic electrochemical experiments and cell testing, you will evaluate how changes in electrolyte composition affect the system's performance and stability. Your work will contribute to a better understanding of the underlying electrochemical mechanisms and help identify promising electrolyte formulations for future energy storage applications.
 Be part of change 
 Conduct electrochemical experiments to investigate the influence of different electrolyte additives and concentrations
 Perform electrochemical measurements and redox flow battery cell tests
 Evaluate and interpret experimental data to assess electrochemical performance
 Investigate the influence of electrolyte composition on iron redox reactions and relevant side reactions
 Review relevant scientific literature
 Document and present your findings in a scientific thesis
 What you contribute 
 Background in electrochemistry, chemistry, chemi-cal engineering, materials science or a related field
 Interest in energy-storage technologies and redox-flow batteries
 Experience or interest in electrochemical techniques (CV, EIS, EQCM, etc)
 Experience with LabView is a plus
 Careful and systematic experimental work
 Ability to analyze and interpret experimental data
 Interest in developing a mechanistic understanding of electrochemical processes
 Independent working style and willingness to work in an interdisciplinary research environment
 What we offer 
 A challenging, attractive, interdisciplinary and international working environment
 An appreciative and supportive working atmosphere
 Opportunities for individual professional development
 Flexible working hours through a flexitime arrangement
 Parking facilities, a cafeteria and a library on campus
 … and much more!
 The weekly working hours are up to 20 hours and can be arranged flexibly by mutual agreement. 
 Please submit the following documents: 
 CV
 Current certificate of enrollment
 Current transcript of records
 Place of work: Pfinztal near Karlsruhe 
 With its focus on developing key technologies that are vital for the future and enabling the commercial utilization of this work by business and industry, Fraunhofer plays a central role in the innovation process. As a pioneer and catalyst for groundbreaking developments and scientific excellence, Fraunhofer helps shape society now and in the future.  
 Ready for a change? Then apply now and make a difference! Once we have received your online application, you will receive an automatic confirmation of receipt. We will then get back to you as soon as possible and let you know what happens next.

 WIR MACHEN AUS KLEINEN STRUKTUREN GROSSE INNOVATIONEN – UND AUS IDEEN WIRKLICHKEIT 
VERÄNDERUNG STARTET MIT UNS.
 Am Fraunhofer-Institut für Mikrotechnik und Mikrosysteme IMM entwickeln wir seit über 30 Jahren innovative Lösungen im Mikrobereich. Saubere Energie, Nachhaltigkeit und Gesundheit sind unsere strategischen Forschungsthemen. Wir beschäftigen uns mit Fragen von hoher gesellschaftlicher Relevanz –beispielsweise beschleunigen und miniaturisieren wir diagnostische Tests, verbessern die Zuverlässigkeit dezentraler Energieversorgung oder gestalten nachhaltige chemische Prozesse. Gemeinsam erschließen wir kontinuierlich neue Innovationsfelder und treiben richtungsweisende Entwicklungen voran. Sind Sie dabei?

Dann freuen wir uns über Ihre Initiativbewerbung, z. B. als Doktorand*in, wissenschaftliche*r Mitarbeiter*in, Laborant*in, Ingenieur*in oder Techniker*in. Ausführliche Informationen über unseren Geschäftsbereich Mobile & Dezentrale Wasserstofftechnik finden Sie hier . Bitte geben Sie in Ihrer aussagekräftigen Bewerbung an, welches der genannten Fachgebiete Sie besonders anspricht.

 Wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium oder eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung im naturwissenschaftlich-technischen Bereich, vorzugsweise in der Fachrichtung Verfahrenstechnik, Chemieingenieurwesen, Energietechnik oder verwandten Fachgebieten
 Fundiertes Know-how im gewünschten Themengebiet, idealerweise verbunden mit Berufserfahrung
 Mündliche und schriftliche Kommunikationssicherheit in sehr gutem Deutsch und Englisch

 Spitzenforschung in einer breiten Vielfalt wegweisender Leuchtturmprojekte mit hohem Industrie- und Praxisbezug, die Gesellschaft und Wirtschaft – und Sie selbst – weiterbringen

items.jobTitle: Kraftfahrzeugmechatroniker/in mit dem Schwerpunkt Nutzfahrzeugtechnik (m/w/d) - Semi Berlin
items.jobDescription:
## Möchtest du dazu beitragen, eine Welt nachhaltigen Wohlstands zu schaffen?  
## Dann bewirb dich jetzt als Mobiler Kfz-Mechatroniker/Automechaniker (m/w/d). 
Du bist **KFZ- oder NFZ-TechnikerIn** und willst mehr als Werkstattalltag? 
Wir suchen erfahrene Service-Technikerinnen, die mit uns das Semi Service Programm aufbauen. Ob du schon Heavy-Duty-Erfahrung mitbringst oder bereit bist, in die Nutzfahrzeugwelt einzusteigen: Du arbeitest direkt am Tesla Semi, bringst Produkt und Service weiter – und bist für unsere kommerziellen Kunden der Ansprechpartner vor Ort.
# Wir bieten
- Karriereentwicklung und Weiterbildung: Bei Tesla hast du die Möglichkeit zu persönlichem und beruflichem Wachstum durch regelmäßige Leistungsbeurteilungen, gezielte Trainingsprogramme und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten (z. B. Hochvolt-Schulungen, Management-Trainings).
- Unternehmenskultur: Tauche ein in unsere inspirierende Unternehmenskultur, in der Innovation, Teamarbeit und Leidenschaft im Vordergrund stehen.
- Innovative Projekte und Technologien: Du hast die Chance, an bahnbrechenden Projekten und Technologien zu arbeiten, die die Zukunft der Automobilindustrie und nachhaltiger Energie gestalten.
- Benefits und Vorteile: Dich erwartet ein wettbewerbsfähiges Vergütungs- und Leistungspaket, das Tesla-Aktien oder eine Barprämie, Zugang zu unserem Corporate-Benefits-Programm, 30 Urlaubstage, ein 13. Monatsgehalt, eine Urban Sports Card sowie die Möglichkeit zu betrieblichen Altersvorsorgebeiträgen und einem Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket umfasst.
- Engagiertes Team und positive Arbeitsatmosphäre: Arbeite in einem engagierten und motivierten Team, das sich durch eine tolle Atmosphäre und exzellente Teamarbeit auszeichnet. Sei Teil eines Teams, das dazu beiträgt, eine Welt nachhaltigen Wohlstands aufzubauen.
# **Deine Aufgaben**
- **Produktfeedback an Engineering:** Als Service-TechnikerIn arbeitest du eng mit Engineering und Entwicklung zusammen. Du diagnostizierst den Tesla Semi im Einsatz und gibst praxisnahes Feedback aus Werkstatt und Außendienst – direkt von der Diagnose und Reparatur ins Produkt.
- **Aufbau des Semi-Service im Außendienst:** Du gehörst zu den ersten NFZ-Service-TechnikerInnen für den Tesla Semi im Heavy-Duty-Bereich. Du setzt Standards für Diagnose, Reparatur und Werkzeuge und gestaltest mit, wie der Außendienst später skaliert.
- **Flottenservice Tesla Semi:** Du betreust die Tesla-eigene Semi-Flotte, die Fracht zwischen unseren Fabriken transportiert – typische Lkw- und Nutzfahrzeugtechnik, plus Hochvolt und Telemetrie.
- **Kundenservice, Diagnose und Reparatur:** Du unterstützt Tesla Heavy Service Centers und die ersten Semi-Kunden. Du führst Fehlerdiagnose, Instandsetzung und Wartung an Nutzfahrzeugflotten durch – in der Werkstatt und mobil vor Ort.
- **Vor-Ort-Einsatz beim Kunden:** Du fährst zu Speditionen und Flottenbetreibern und arbeitest mit deren KFZ- und NFZ-TechnikerInnen in der Kundenwerkstatt. Mobile Service, Hands-on, kein Schreibtischjob.
- **Technische Dokumentation:** Du erstellst und pflegst Reparaturanleitungen, Service-Dokumente und Checklisten, mit denen andere Semi-TechnikerInnen den Tesla Semi warten und reparieren können.
- **Ladesupport und Hochvolt**: Du unterstützt Kunden bei Ladeproblemen, Ladeinfrastruktur und Hochvolt-Themen am Semi – von der Fehlersuche bis zur Lösung vor Ort.
# Dein Profil
- **Führerschein**: Du hast einen gültigen Führerschein Klasse B und bist bereit, die Klasse C bzw. CE zu erwerben – wichtig für den Einsatz am Tesla Semi und im Heavy-Duty-Außendienst.
- **Technische Expertise:** Du bringst Erfahrung in Diagnose, Fehlerbehebung und Reparatur von Fahrzeugsystemen mit – Motor, Getriebe, Niedervolt- und Hochvolt-Elektrik. OEM-Schulungen, ASE-Zertifizierungen sowie 608/609-Zertifizierungen sind von Vorteil, ebenso KFZ-, NFZ- oder Lkw-Technik.
- **Problemlösung und Teamarbeit**: Du diagnostizierst komplexe Fehler, denkst praxisnah und arbeitest eng mit anderen TechnikerInnen zusammen. Du kommunizierst klar mit Kunden und hältst im kommerziellen Service den Überblick.
- **Arbeitsbedingungen**: Du arbeitest auch unter nicht klimatisierten Bedingungen – in der Werkstatt, in der Kundenhalle und im Außendienst.
- **Flexibilität und Reisebereitschaft**: Du bist bereit, zu Kunden, in nahe Regionen und zu Schulungsorten zu reisen, den geforderten Arbeitsplan einzuhalten und am Einsatzort zu arbeiten. Umzugsbereitschaft je nach Programmbedarf ist von Vorteil.
#

We Say HI*
Embedded Software Engineer (m/f/d):
 Your Mission:
 Design, develop, implement and test embedded software features, ensuring scalability, performance, reliability and maintainability.
 Develop high-quality, reusable and efficient code following software engineering best practices.
 Work on real-time and embedded systems deployed on devices such as radar systems, smartcards, wearable technologies, embedded computing platforms and IoT solutions.
 Contribute to the integration, validation and testing of software solutions through the development and adaptation of simulation tools and test environments.
 Support troubleshooting and issue investigation activities across development, testing and integration environments.
 Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary teams, including software engineers, system engineers, DevOps specialists and UX teams, to deliver robust and user-centric solutions.
 Follow Agile methodologies, participating in sprint planning, user story creation, task definition and continuous improvement activities.
 Apply security and software quality best practices throughout the software development lifecycle.
 Stay up to date with emerging technologies, frameworks and industry best practices within embedded and real-time software engineering.
 What We Are Looking For:
 Master's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering or a related technical field.
 Previous professional experience in embedded software development and real-time systems.
 Strong programming skills in one or more languages such as: C, C++, Ada, Assembly and/or .NET technologies.
 Experience developing software on embedded operating systems such as: Linux, VxWorks, FastOS Linux or similar platforms.
 Experience with communication protocols and interfaces such as DDS, ARINC or comparable technologies.
 Hands-on experience with software integration, testing and validation activities, including the development and maintenance of simulation tools and test environments.
 Familiarity with measurement, diagnostic and instrumentation tools used for software and hardware verification.
 Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
 Experience using Agile development methodologies and collaboration tools such as Jira and Confluence.
 Customer-focused mindset with strong communication and collaboration skills.
 Interest in developing solutions that bridge low-level hardware interaction with high-level software functionality.
 Previous experience within industries such as Telecommunications, IoT, Aerospace, Defense, Transportation or other mission-critical environments (plus).

About the AI Security Institute
 The AI Security Institute is the world's largest and best-funded team dedicated to understanding advanced AI risks and translating that knowledge into action. We’re in the heart of the UK government with direct lines to No. 10 (the Prime Minister's office), and we work with frontier developers and governments globally.
 We’re here because governments are critical for advanced AI going well, and UK AISI is uniquely positioned to mobilise them. With our resources, unique agility and international influence, this is the best place to shape both AI development and government action.
 The deadline for applying to this role is Tuesday 8th December,  end of day, anywhere on Earth 
 About the team 
 The Red Team conducts cutting-edge research to identify, evaluate and stress test vulnerabilities in frontier AI systems, sharing our findings directly with leading AI companies, UK officials and allied governments. Our work shapes how the most powerful AI systems are deployed - you can read about it in the The New York Times , The Economist,  and The Telegraph . Demand for this work is growing faster than we can currently meet - we're scaling to address that gap. 
 The Red Team’s work is crucial to ensuring advanced AI systems are developed and deployed safely. We are composed of three specialised sub-teams:    
 Misuse : stress-testing and jailbreaking safeguards against misuse of dangerous capabilities (e.g. our safeguard testing with Anthropic and OpenAI, and recent work on Boundary Point Jailbreaking , attacks on layered safeguard systems and principles for evaluating misuse safeguards ) 
 Alignment : detecting and understanding misalignment and loss-of-control risks (e.g., our evaluation of GPT-6 Astra , and our research into cheating behaviour in frontier model evaluations ) 
 Control :  stress-testing measures that identify and prevent agents taking harmful actions   
 While each team has its own focus, we share methodologies, infrastructure and tooling across the wider team.  
 Role Description   
 We are looking for motivated and talented Software Engineers to join the Red Team. We are seeking exceptional candidates at all experience levels, from junior through to senior, staff and principal levels. 
 We are particularly interested in candidates who: 
 Have worked closely with research teams, understanding their needs, building tools they want to use, and automating their workflows. 
 Have a good understanding of frontier AI capabilities, limitations, and risks and how they can be leveraged for automation at scale. 
 Have built infrastructure that works at scale, with a high bar for security.  
 Have experience with serving and training models.
 What you’ll be doing 
 As a software engineer on one of our sub teams, you might:  
 Build and maintain systems for running red-teaming against frontier models at scale, such as automated jailbreaking pipelines, alignment auditor agents in Inspect Petri, and attacker agents for control red-teaming 
 Design and implement systems for running large scale automated research and engineering with many agents on AISI’s research platform 
 Extend our evaluation tooling, built on Inspect (AISI's open-source framework for evaluating AI), to new kinds of targets 
 Develop novel solutions to performance, reliability, and security problems that arise from running thousands of agents in parallel 
 Work with Core Technology to share infrastructure and avoid duplicating work 
 Help run pre-release testing of frontier models, often to tight deadlines 
 Debug problems as they come up and make sure results are reliable and reproducible 
 Turn loosely defined research ideas into well-tested, documented and maintainable code 
 Review code, share knowledge and help researchers write better software 
 Person specification  
 You may be a good fit if you have some of the following skills, experience and attitudes: 
 Writing production quality code at fast pace. 
 Interest in developing ways to automate work with agents, while accounting for their limitations. 
 Designing, shipping, and maintaining complex tech products. 
 Improving technical standards across a team, through mentoring and feedback. 
 Strong written and verbal communication skills. 
 Collaborating effectively with many people, including external teams. 
 Experience working with a world-class research team comprised of both scientists and engineers (e.g. in a top-3 lab). 
 Python experience 
 Experience building and maintaining systems on AWS or other cloud providers using infrastructure-as-code. 
 Highly Desirable 
 We additionally may factor in experience with particular areas like: 
 Expertise in Cloud Infrastructure or Dev Ops (AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, Terraform, CDK, Docker, etc.) 
 Cybersecurity expertise 
 ML Ops (vLLM, agent frameworks, fine-tuning, RAG systems, etc.) 
 Experience with red teaming, adversarial machine learning, or offensive or adversarial security (for example penetration testing or capture-the-flag competitions) 
 Hands-on experience with large language model APIs and the tools around them, such as OpenAI-compatible APIs, agent frameworks or vLLM 
 Building, running or analysing AI evaluations, ideally with Inspect 
 Cloud infrastructure and DevOps experience with AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform or similar 
 Familiarity with how AI could be misused or could slip out of human control, and how safeguards try to prevent this 
 This might not be the role for you if:
 You prefer working on production-grade software and would find rapid prototyping or "good enough for now" code frustrating
 You prefer well-defined requirements and long planning cycles. Our priorities shift as new models are released, and our projects often run to tight deadlines. 
 Selection  process 
 The interview process may vary from candidate to candidate, however, you should expect a typical process to include some technical proficiency tests, discussions with a cross-section of our team at AISI (including non-technical staff) and conversations with your team lead. The process will culminate in a conversation with members of the senior leadership team here at AISI.       
 Candidates should expect to go through  some or all of the following stages once an application has been submitted:       
 Initial assessment    
 Initial screening call      
 Technical assessment   
 Behavioural interview    
 Final interview with members of the senior leadership team
 What We Offer   
 Impact you couldn't have anywhere else   
 Incredibly talented, mission-driven and supportive colleagues.   
 Direct influence on how frontier AI is governed and deployed globally.   
 Work with the Prime Minister’s AI Advisor and leading AI companies.   
 Opportunity to shape the first & best-resourced public-interest research team focused on AI security.   
 Resources & access   
 Pre-release access to multiple frontier models and ample compute.   
 Extensive operational support so you can focus on research and ship quickly.   
 Work with experts across national security, policy, AI research and adjacent sciences.   
 Growth & autonomy   
 If you’re talented and driven, you’ll own important problems early.   
 5 days off and annual stipends for learning and development, and funding for conferences and external collaborations.   
 Freedom to pursue research bets without product pressure.   
 Opportunities to publish and collaborate externally.   
 Life & family*   
 Modern central London office, or where applicable, option to work in similar government offices in Birmingham, Cardiff, Darlington, Edinburgh, Salford or Bristol.   
 Hybrid working, flexibility for occasional remote work abroad and stipends for work-from-home equipment.   
 At least 25 days’ annual leave, 8 public holidays, extra team-wide breaks and 3 days off for volunteering.   
 Generous paid parental leave (36 weeks of UK statutory leave shared between parents + 3 extra paid weeks + option for additional unpaid time).   
 Excellent pension provision, with a choice between Partnership (no employee contributions required and up to 14.75% employer contributions) or Alpha, a valuable defined benefit scheme that provides a guaranteed, inflation-linked retirement income for life. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window). 
 Discounts and benefits for cycling to work, donations and retail/gyms.  
 *These benefits apply to direct employees. Benefits may differ for individuals joining through other employment arrangements such as secondments.   
 Salary 
 Annual salary is benchmarked to role scope and relevant experience. Most offers land between £65,000 and £145,000 made up of a base salary plus a technical allowance (take-home salary = base + technical allowance).  
 This role sits outside of the  DDaT pay framework  given the scope of this role requires in depth technical expertise in frontier AI safety, robustness and advanced AI architectures.   
 The full range of salaries are available below:   
 Level 3: £65,000–£75,000 (Base £40,850 + Technical Allowance £24,150–£34,150)
 Level 4: £85,000–£95,000 (Base £48,540 + Technical Allowance £36,460–£46,460)
 Level 5: £105,000–£115,000 (Base £63,165 + Technical Allowance £41,835–£51,835)
 Level 6: £125,000–£135,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £48,525–£58,525)
 Level 7: £145,000 (Base £76,475 + Technical Allowance £68,525)
 Additional Information
 Use of AI in Applications 
 Artificial Intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our  candidate guidance  for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.
 Use of AI tools in recruitment 
We may use AI tools to help our hiring team review applications, for example by summarising application materials and helping us prioritise them against the published criteria. We do not use AI tools to find information about you from other sources, including online. People make every decision. We do not make solely automated decisions about candidates. Find out more, including your rights, in our recruitment privacy notice: https://www.aisi.gov.uk/careers/privacy-policy.
 Internal Fraud Database   
 The Internal Fraud function of the Fraud, Error, Debt and Grants Function at the Cabinet Office processes details of civil servants who have been dismissed for committing internal fraud, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned. The Cabinet Office receives the details from participating government organisations of civil servants who have been dismissed, or who would have been dismissed had they not resigned, for internal fraud. In instances such as this, civil servants are then banned for 5 years from further employment in the civil service. The Cabinet Office then processes this data and discloses a limited dataset back to DLUHC as a participating government organisations. DLUHC then carry out the pre employment checks so as to detect instances where known fraudsters are attempting to reapply for roles in the civil service. In this way, the policy is ensured and the repetition of internal fraud is prevented.  For more information please see -  Internal Fraud Register. 
 Security 
 Successful candidates must undergo a criminal record check and get  baseline personnel security standard (BPSS) clearance  before they can be appointed. Additionally, there is a strong preference for eligibility for  counter-terrorist check (CTC) clearance . Some roles may require higher levels of clearance, and we will state this by exception in the job advertisement.  See our vetting charter here. 
 Nationality requirements 
 We may be able to offer roles to applicant from any nationality or background . As such we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet the standard nationality requirements (opens in a new window). 
 Working for the Civil Service 
 The  Civil Service Code (opens in a new window) sets out the standards of behaviour expected of civil servants. The Civil Service embraces diversity and promotes equal opportunities. About Alta Ares
Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.
 Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
 Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.
 The challenge 
We build the ground equipment that keeps our interceptor drones connected, and it must be set up fast by a single operator in harsh field conditions. Mechanics decide whether antennas stay on target and whether electronics survive transport, weather and rough handling. You will go from CAD to prototypes to field tests, working hands-on with RF, electrical and operations colleagues.
 Missions 
 Design an antenna positioning system: drive train, cable management, stiffness and wind resistance.
 Design rugged enclosures for radio modules and electronics: sealing, thermal management, mounting.
 Evaluate off-the-shelf solutions: compare commercial positioners and mounts against our needs and support buy-vs-build decisions.
 Build modularity into the ground equipment: common interfaces, quick set-up, easy maintenance.
 Take parts from prototype to production: 3D printing to machined parts, drawings, mechanical BOM, assembly instructions.
 Support field trials and deployments: set-up, feedback from operators, design fixes.
 Required skills 
 Engineering degree in mechanical or mechatronics engineering, with experience designing electromechanical products.
 Solid mechanism design fundamentals: tolerancing, gears and reductions, bearings, structural and wind-load calculations.
 CAD (Fusion 360 or SolidWorks), design for manufacturing and assembly, rapid prototyping (3D printing, CNC).
 Rugged outdoor design (sealing, thermal, vibration); experience with antenna trackers, gimbals, drones or defense equipment is a plus.
 Working knowledge of motion systems (motors, encoders, drives) to collaborate with electrical and software teams.
 Hands-on and autonomous, available for frequent field trials and travel.

About Watershed
 Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.
 We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!
 The role
 Forward Deployed Energy Engineers are a new role at Watershed, combining energy and advisory expertise with product-building skills and commercial instinct. You’ll operate at the cutting edge with Watershed customers to build and deploy the next generation of enterprise energy management.
 Energy is one of the largest costs on a big company’s P&L and one of its largest sources of emissions. Yet most enterprises have no one who owns how energy is purchased, consumed and reduced across all their sites. Watershed is building the product that changes that, and it’s the company’s biggest bet for its next chapter.
 We already help many of the world’s largest companies measure and cut their emissions, and our clean energy business has executed more than $100M in purchases. Now we’re building energy management from zero to one, with engagements underway with a small group of customers today and scaling in 2027.
 You’ll work with enterprises that spend tens of millions a year on electricity, embedded in their energy programmes. Starting from the energy data already in Watershed, you’ll find where they’re overspending, deliver the savings, prototype with AI what should become product, and help customers implement solutions, including buying clean power. The goal is an energy programme that wins backing from their CFO and facilities teams. This is a high-ownership role on a small, high-output team, with a direct line to commercial outcomes and real say in what we build. It reports directly to Watershed’s head of energy and decarbonization.
 What you'll do 
 Deliver energy engagements with measurable results: Run deep engagements with a handful of customers at a time: change tariffs, upgrade equipment, find and cut waste, and show the savings.
 Win customers who vouch for us: Earn the trust of facilities and finance leads so they would tell a peer to work with Watershed.
 Turn what works into product: Spot the problems that repeat across customers, prototype with AI, and work with our engineers to build an AI-led product for many.
 Close clean energy deals: Help customers sign deals with existing clean power products (eg EACs, fixed-price VPPAs), yourself or alongside our account teams.
 Make the team smarter on energy: Be the person colleagues go to on tariffs, loads and what actually cuts a bill.
 You might be a fit if you 
 Know how commercial and industrial sites use and buy energy (tariffs, loads, HVAC and controls, procurement) from time at an ESCO, an energy consultancy, an engineering firm or an energy-tech company.
 Have built things: scripts, models, prototypes or AI-assisted workflows, and can show us one. Prototype-quality code is enough; moving fast matters most.
 Are fluent with data tools (Excel, SQL or Python) and LLM tools, and can turn messy meter and bill data into something a customer acts on.
 Have run client work from scoping to outcome, and are as credible with a facilities manager as with a CFO.
 Can tell a compelling story with data, from raw numbers to insight to a recommendation someone signs off. You've originated work or supported deals, and want to get better at selling.
 Are energised to build a new product and service, to be on the front lines of building a new business, and to leave a legacy as part of a fast-moving team.
 Nice to have 
 Experience with clean power deals (PPAs, VPPAs, fixed-price power contracts, and energy attribute certificates like RECs, GOs and REGOs).
 Hands-on work with utility bill, half-hourly or building management system data.
 A few years in consulting or advisory.
 Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) 
 Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.
 What’s the interview process like? 
 It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.
 What if I need accommodations for my interview? 
 At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.
