About Us 
 Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.
 Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.
 About the Role 
 As a confirmed Radar Signal Processing Engineer on Harmattan AI's Radar team in Paris, you will own the signal processing algorithms behind our next-generation airborne radar payload. You will take full ownership of your workstream, from algorithmic research through embedded implementation and flight validation, working with high autonomy and minimal oversight. You will work closely with the EW and RF analytics teams to translate product-level requirements into deployed, mission-ready capabilities.
 Responsibilities 
 Design and implement near-real-time algorithms for radar image formation, including inverse SAR (ISAR) processing of moving targets.
 Develop and refine detection and tracking algorithms (e.g., EKF/UKF-based approaches) for moving target indication on airborne radar data.
 Build jamming estimation capabilities, combining out-of-band spectral sniffing with in-band spatial covariance analysis, and the adaptive logic that drives radar behavior in response.
 Contribute radar-derived observables and algorithms that support navigation when GNSS is unavailable.
 Prototype and port algorithms onto the selected embedded computing platform, balancing algorithmic performance against real-time and resource constraints.
 Validate algorithms end-to-end through hardware-in-the-loop bench testing, anechoic chamber campaigns, and real flight conditions, iterating quickly on results.
 Work closely with the EW and RF analytics modules to align signal processing development with system-level requirements.
 Candidate Requirements
 2 to 5 years of confirmed, hands-on experience in radar signal processing, gained in the defense or automotive radar industry preferably.
 Solid experience in Signal Processing on radar systems, either FMCW or pulsed, is required; exposure to moving target tracking, ECCM, radar-based navigation, or live/real-time processing is a strong plus.
 Strong theoretical foundations and genuine hands-on comfort with the underlying mathematics, not reliance on off-the-shelf tools or LLM-generated solutions.
 A quick thinker, comfortable taking full ownership of a technical scope end-to-end with minimal oversight.
 Comfortable working in a fast, iterative cycle: writing code, running hardware-in-the-loop tests, and pushing validated changes independently.
 We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

About THG Ingenuity   
 THG Ingenuity is a proprietary Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) technology, robotics, and operations platform built for global ecommerce. Developed through more than two decades of operating ecommerce and retail services at scale, its software and automation capabilities have been engineered, tested, and refined through the real-world demands of managing complex commerce operations. Today, THG Ingenuity provides an integrating operating environment that enables brands to intelligently optimise the entire commerce lifecycle from browsing and checkout to AI inventory management and forecasting, automated fulfilment, carrier control, and customer experience. The platform comprises:   
 THG Fulfil: The fulfilment operating system for global ecommerce. Delivered via a proprietary SaaS and Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model, THG Fulfil orchestrates every stage of checkout, fulfilment, delivery, and customer experience through an integrated system.   
 THG Studios: The UK's most innovative creative hub, helping brands create content that connects, experiences that engage, and IP that scales, all from its end-to-end, in-house facilities.    
 THG Commerce: A cloud-native technology stack enabling retailers and brands to create intelligent, AI-powered, digital shopping experiences, while integrated marketplace and social commerce functionality allows brands to reach customers across every sales channel   
 With its expertise in building and scaling brands, THG Ingenuity is uniquely positioned to bring pertinent, pragmatic, and global know-how across all aspects of commerce.   
 The Role 
 We are seeking a talented and commercially astute Data Scientist to join our dynamic team tackling Fraud, Payments and Finance. In this multi-focus role, you will be responsible for protecting our global e-commerce operations from fraud, optimising our payments performance and driving profitability and automation initiatives within Finance.
 Working with vast, complex datasets, the work will involve combatting online fraud using our award-winning THG Detect platform and driving payments optimisation by increasing authorisation rates, while also using the latest AI software and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) infrastructure to build complex data solutions and applications.
 This role requires a blend of strong technical skills, commercial acumen, and effective communication to translate complex data insights into tangible business value.
 Responsibilities: 
 Optimise Fraud Detection:  Continuously improve automated decision-making in our in-house THG Detect platform using machine learning and decision rules.
 Enhance Payment Performance:  Lead data-driven initiatives to boost payment authorisation rates, optimise transaction routing, and reduce costs.
 Drive Profitability within Finance:  Lead automation and profitability initiatives across different areas of Finance.
 Communicate Performance:  Report on all aspects of fraud, payments and finance performance to stakeholders at all levels, including C-level management.
 Drive System Improvements:  Collaborate with Fraud, Payments, Finance and Engineering teams to scope and implement enhancements to detection systems and data pipelines.
 Innovate & Automate:  Proactively identify opportunities to improve detection capabilities, drive profitability, increase payment success, and enhance team efficiency through automation.
 Requirements: 
 Proficient with SQL & Python
 Proficient in a data visualisation software (Tableau/Looker/PowerBI/e.t.c.)
 Experience using a variety of machine learning algorithms
 Able to communicate effectively; using data to tell a story and drive business change
 Experience within Google Cloud preferential

About us
 We are building a global leader in physical AI, anchored in Europe’s strongest robotics heritage. Founded by entrepreneurs with backgrounds in scaling digital products and advanced robotics, the team is bolstered by senior leadership from top-tier AI research labs and industrial tech companies.
 Driven by a mission to create versatile and trustworthy embodied AI for physical labor, we fuse deep engineering mastery in AI and mechatronics with a rapid-execution culture. We are addressing the labor shortage by closing the gap to production-grade deployment. This means building the trusted alternative: robots that are safe, secure, and engineered to automotive standards of scale and durability.
 We are well-capitalized and now assembling our team.
 Our Locations: Vesoma has two main locations: Munich, Germany and Limassol, Cyprus. This pan-European setup represents our core ambition of building a European technology leader, gives us a great talent base and a strong corporate structure.
 Your mission 
 As a Robot Operations Engineer , you will be the backbone of our hands-on robotic development. You will be responsible for the bring-up of fresh hardware, maintaining our active hardware fleet, as well as owning the "robot gym": our dedicated lab environment where robots undergo continuous testing and AI model training.
 Your work ensures that our AI and software teams have uninterrupted access to high-functioning, reliable hardware. Working at the intersection of hardware engineering and AI development, you will oversee prototype bring-up, diagnose electromechanical issues, and create a structured, highly efficient lab environment that accelerates our overall product development cycle.
 Key responsibilities 
 Hardware Bring-up : Perform the initial bringing up and commissioning of freshly built prototypes. Ensure the flawless interaction between hardware, firmware, and base software stacks before handing them over for active testing.
 "Robot Gym" Management : Own and operate the "robot gym." Ensure the lab environment is safe, organized, and continuously optimized to support the AI team's data collection and training operations.
 Fleet & Inventory Ownership : Track, maintain, and manage the entire inventory of robot prototypes, sub-assemblies, and critical spare parts. Ensure all active units are properly version-controlled and running the latest hardware and firmware configurations.
 Maintenance & Troubleshooting : Perform routine maintenance, sensor calibrations, and hands-on repairs across the robot fleet. Rapidly diagnose and resolve electromechanical, networking, or system-level issues to minimize testing downtime.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration : Act as the primary technical bridge between the Hardware and AI teams. Provide operational support, manage hardware allocation requests, and feed critical performance observations back to the hardware engineering team to improve future iterations.
 Process Standardization : Establish and document clear standard operating procedures (SOPs) for robot operation, safety protocols, lab maintenance, and hardware troubleshooting.
 Your profile 
 We are looking for hands-on engineers who love getting their hands dirty with complex mechatronic systems and take immense pride in keeping a high-tech robotic fleet running at peak performance.
 Experience : 3+ years of experience in robotics operations, lab management, hardware testing, field engineering, or a similar hands-on electromechanical role.
 Core Skills : Strong hands-on mechanical and electrical troubleshooting capabilities. Familiarity with Linux environments, basic network configuration, and scripting (e.g., Python or Bash) for system diagnostics and bring-up. Experience managing hardware inventory, using standard lab equipment, and ensuring operational safety.
 Mindset : You are highly organized, proactive, and service-oriented. You thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced lab environment, possess a strong sense of ownership over your fleet, and understand that the success of our AI development relies heavily on the readiness and reliability of the hardware you manage.
 Why us?
 The Team : Work alongside leadership with a proven track record of building unicorn-scale companies and defining global robotics standards.
 Smart Strategy : We operate as disciplined fast followers. Capital is timed to the deployment inflection point, avoiding early-mover dead ends to scale fast on proven foundations.
 Resources : We are substantially internally funded and attract top-tier investors to avoid any capital constraints for our mission.
 Historic Opportunity : Join at the dawn of a new industry comparable to the rise of the automobile. Help shape the European champion in this trillion-dollar market.
 We are an equal opportunity employer.

This is a dedicated infrastructure, security, and platform role, and there's a lot of ground to claim. Right now a handful of engineers keep the whole stack running between them. Your job is to turn that into something that runs and scales on purpose, and to make it more secure while you do. The more reliable we are, the more people we help lead healthier, happier lives.
 About Wellis 
 Wellis is a fast-growing healthtech scale-up reinventing healthcare. We are building the first truly integrated health platform in the Netherlands, offering on-demand care for everyday health needs such as weight loss, hair loss, sexual health, and more. Our platform covers the full journey: from diagnosis and medical assessment to prescription and delivery at home. By combining medical expertise, technology, and data, we make healthcare smarter, more accessible, more personal, and easier to use. We are growing quickly, which means we are building the structures, teams, products, and processes that will help us scale responsibly. You will join an ambitious, international team where ownership is encouraged, collaboration is key, and impact is visible from day one.
 The Role 
 You won't inherit a mature platform team here. You'll help build one. Our services already run across more than one cloud, most provisioning still happens by hand, and we have very little visibility into what's actually going on in production. Fixing that is the job: bringing order, portability, and security to all of it, and doing it the way our engineering team already works, which is agent-first.
 The role covers three areas, and we mean all three. On infrastructure, you'll own how and where we run. We want managed services that stay portable, so we can pick up a workload and move it between GCP, AWS, or anywhere else without rewriting it. On security, you'll own access provisioning, database security, secrets, and the controls a company handling patient data has to get right. On IT and platform admin, you'll own onboarding, offboarding, team access, and tooling: the unglamorous plumbing that keeps a growing team moving.
 What ties the three together is automation. We're not looking for someone to click through consoles all day. We're looking for someone who builds the systems and agents that make provisioning, deployment, and access self-serve.
 We're an AI-native engineering team. Agentic coding tools are how we work, and infrastructure is no exception. Think Terraform written and reviewed with an agent, runbooks that are actually scripts, an access request that a workflow fulfills on its own. You'll bring that habit to a corner of the company that usually gets it last.
 What You'll Own 
 Provider-agnostic infrastructure. Define our infra as code so it's reproducible and portable. Containerize workloads, standardize how services get deployed, and keep us free to move between clouds instead of locked into one. Today we run across more than one provider mostly by accident. You'll make it a choice. 
 CI/CD and release engineering. Build the pipelines that take code from merge to production safely: automated, repeatable, with the guardrails that let a small team ship often without breaking things.
 Observability and reliability. We have almost no monitoring, alerting, or error tracking today. You'll build the visibility layer from scratch, from metrics and logs through tracing, uptime, and the basics of on-call, so we catch problems before customers do.
 Security and access. Own IAM and least-privilege access across our systems, plus database hardening, secrets management, and the audit trails a regulated healthcare business needs. Access for people and services should be controlled and reviewable, never handed out ad hoc.
 Team provisioning and IT admin, automated. Onboarding, offboarding, accounts, and tooling access, built as workflows and agents rather than a ticket queue. When someone joins or leaves, the right things should happen without a person doing them by hand.
 Infrastructure agents and tooling. Build the skills, scripts, and agent workflows that let the whole team self-serve infra and access. This is the leverage that lets a small team run like a bigger one.
 What we offer 
 Salary range €5,500 – €8,000 gross per month, depending on experience, plus 8% holiday allowance
 Pension plan
 Learning budget
 Monthly personal budget (Alleo)
 Hybrid working: partly from our new office in central Rotterdam (2 days)
 20 days of remote working per year
 Working from home allowance (2 days a week)
 25 holidays
 A culture of short lines, speed, and continuous improvement, where pragmatism and impact matter
 The chance to build a healthtech scale-up's entire infrastructure and security foundation from the ground up
 Essential 
 3+ years of professional DevOps, platform, SRE, or infrastructure engineering. You've owned production infrastructure, not just touched it. Fundamentals matter more than years here: what happens on deploy, how to recover, how to keep it running.
 Infrastructure as code, done properly. Terraform, Pulumi, OpenTofu, or equivalent. You provision through version control, not a console, and you know why that discipline matters.
 Cloud, with an eye on portability. Real experience with at least one major cloud (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and the container tooling (Docker, plus Kubernetes or a managed equivalent) that keeps workloads movable. You've thought about lock-in and how to avoid it.
 CI/CD ownership. You've built and maintained pipelines that other engineers depend on, with the automated checks and rollbacks that make frequent deploys safe.
 Security fundamentals. IAM and access control, secrets management, network basics, and database security. You know how to give people and services exactly the access they need and nothing more.
 Agentic AI development is how you work. You spend a real part of your day in tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Pi, or opencode, and you point them at infrastructure and ops, not just app code. Given a repetitive task, your instinct is to automate it. 
 You've felt the pain. A migration that locked a table, a deploy that took down an endpoint, an access mistake you had to clean up at 2am. You owned it, fixed it, and built the guardrail so it couldn't happen twice.
 Nice to Have 
 Building agents and agentic workflows, not just using them: plugins, skills, or custom automations that made infra or ops better for a team.
 Experience with regulated or sensitive data (healthcare, financial services, government). You know why 'move fast and break things' has no place near patient data.
 Observability tooling stood up from scratch: Sentry, Prometheus and Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, or similar.
 IT administration at a growing company: SSO and identity providers, device and access lifecycle, automated on and offboarding.
 Audit logging and compliance in regulated environments (NEN 7513, GDPR, ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar).
 Running Supabase, Postgres, or serverless and edge platforms (Cloud Run, edge functions) in production.
 Multi-cloud or cloud-migration experience, meaning you've moved real workloads between providers.
 Dutch and/or German (business English is the working language).
 Who You Are 
 You take ownership from provisioning through deployment through monitoring, right up to the 2am page.
 You automate by instinct. Do something twice by hand and you're already writing the thing that does it for you.
 You're comfortable being the first and only person in your domain, making decisions that carry weight, with no team to hide behind yet.
 You treat security as the default. You handle access and data like someone's health depends on it, because it does.
 You work fast and stay careful.
 With Your Application 
 Alongside your CV, share a transcript or a detailed walkthrough of the most interesting agentic session you've had recently, one where the agent did real infrastructure, ops, or automation work. Provisioning, a pipeline, a migration, an access workflow, whatever it was. Tell us what you were building, how you steered the agent, and what you'd do differently. We'd rather read that than a cover letter.
 Hiring Process 
 We want the application process at Wellis to be fast, transparent, and personal.
 Introductory chat with Georgios (Senior Recruiter)
 Introductory interview with the CTO. Come ready to talk about a production incident you owned: what broke, what you did, what changed afterwards.
 Technical assessment with the CTO
 Final conversation with founders

 #Jobdrehscheibe

 Sie wollen mit uns Gas geben? Starten Sie durch und bewerben Sie sich jetzt!

items.jobDescription:
What To Expect
 Join the mission to launch Cybercab, Tesla’s revolutionary fully autonomous Robotaxi, on the most advanced automotive manufacturing lines in the world. As a Cybercab Engineer, you won’t just support the lines… you will own them. You become a key individual partnering with cross-functional teams, to execute, and relentlessly optimize processes during the high-stakes ramping phase.
You’ll drive Tesla’s novel manufacturing method, the groundbreaking approach that breaks the vehicle into major modules built in parallel on open, highly accessible stations before final joining. This isn’t traditional automotive manufacturing. This is a radical, high-speed, modular manufacturing revolution, redesigned to shrink footprints, and unlocks blistering production rates.
These lines are loaded with cutting-edge automation and robotics. You’ll lead the deployment of advanced equipment process, focusing on quality/efficiency/safety targets, and execute an aggressive production ramp that few in the industry will ever experience. You’ll turn the most ambitious vehicle Tesla has ever built into reality at scale.
This is an opportunity to own world-class lines, master Unboxed manufacturing, and help write the next chapter of the automotive history.
 What You'll Do
 PLC Troubleshooting and Optimization: Diagnose and resolve PLC faults to minimize downtime, improve cycle times, and enhance process efficiency 
 Equipment Integration: Seamlessly install, program, and integrate new equipment, including robotics, sensors, and dispense systems, into existing automated lines 
 Programming and Commissioning: Configure and program IO devices, servo systems, Fanuc robots, and vision systems to meet process and production needs 
 System Improvements: Modify PLC Controls sequence logic, robot sequence and vision programs, and other system controls to enhance safety, reliability, reduce faults, and achieve production goals. HMI software updates to optimize equipment operator experience 
 Equipment Electrical updates: Review and update electrical wiring diagrams, layout drawings for VFDs, Servos, PLC and other controls devices 
 Support 24/7 Production Operations as needed 
 What You'll Bring
 Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics Engineering, or equivalent experience 
 2+ years with Automotive manufacturing experience as a Controls Engineering role 
 Technical Expertise: Proficiency in PLC programming of Equipment sequences using IEC-61131 complaint programming languages and logic troubleshooting (e.g., Siemens, Allen-Bradley) and hands-on experience with Fanuc robot programming. Proficiency in HMI/SCADA industrial systems (SIMATIC WinCC, TIA Portal or Ignition SCADA). Experience with Motor Drive setup and troubleshooting (SEW EURODrive and Siemens G120, S120 preferred) 
 Electrical Skills: Experience with Electrical Design using EPlan (preferred) or AutoCAD Electrical and Schematic troubleshooting. Demonstrated experience with 3-phase 480/208 VAC, single-phase 208/120 VAC, and 24 VDC systems 
 Industrial Network: knowledge of PROFINET communication protocols 
 Vision and Dispense Systems Knowledge: Familiarity with configuring and optimizing vision systems (Keyence, Cognex) and programming dispense and fluid fill systems. Fanuc 2D IRVision and Fanuc 3DVision experience
 Analytical Skills: Strong problem-solving ability to address complex technical issues, identify root causes, and implement effective solutions

About Boltz 
 Boltz is a public benefit company building the next generation of AI-powered molecular modeling tools to make biology programmable and accelerate drug discovery, while keeping frontier capabilities broadly accessible.
 Boltz was founded by former MIT scientists who created Boltz-1, the first fully commercially available open-source model to approach AlphaFold 3-level accuracy in predicting the 3D structure of biomolecular complexes.
 We focus on two things:
 Foundation models. Our open models, Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and BoltzGen, are trusted by 100,000+ scientists across biotech and academia, and used in programs at every Top 20 pharma as well as leading agrichemical and industrial research organizations. Our latest proprietary foundation models power our products and the custom models we build with partners.
 Boltz Lab and the Boltz API. Our products run our latest models, design pipelines (BoltzMol for small molecules, BoltzProt for protein design) and agents as reliable, production-grade tools built around real chemistry and biology workflows. Teams start from a target and a hypothesis, then generate, evaluate, and rank candidate molecules in Boltz Lab, run our models from their own code and agents through the Boltz API, or deploy them inside their own environment.
 The two feed each other: our open releases earn scientific credibility and community insight, and our products turn our full range of models into real impact for partners including Pfizer, Takeda, GSK, Bristol Myers Squibb and DSM-Firmenich.

 Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.
 We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.
 About the role
 Join Mistral AI’s Defense team to build software for defense institutions and industry.
 We are looking for an experienced software engineer with strong engineering fundamentals and a background in data engineering or transactional, analytical or distributed systems. You will help shape the architecture, write production code and own substantial software components, from design through deployment and operation.
 This role offers the scope and autonomy of a senior technical individual contributor in a small team. It is particularly suited to engineers operating at Senior or Staff level in demanding product engineering environments who want broad ownership and to stay deeply involved in implementation.
 What you will do
 Design and build services for data ingestion, transformation, storage, querying and operational workflows.
 Develop shared data models, APIs and SDKs that help engineers build applications on a consistent foundation.
 Make authorization a core part of the architecture: define and enforce which users, applications and agents can access data or perform actions, with clear audit trails.
 Solve problems involving data consistency, schema evolution, concurrency, performance and failure recovery across services and data systems.
 Turn needs from our applied engineers and defense users into reusable software capabilities, making pragmatic choices about what to build and how to evolve them.
 Own delivery end to end, including implementation, testing, observability, debugging and maintainability in demanding deployment environments.
 Use AI coding tools and coding agents extensively to accelerate implementation, testing, refactoring and debugging. Help the team improve these workflows while maintaining a high engineering standard.
 What we are looking for
 Strong practical familiarity with AI coding tools and agentic engineering workflows. You use coding agents regularly, can break complex work into well-scoped tasks, provide effective context, review generated code and validate the result through tests and debugging. You remain accountable for the architecture, correctness, security and maintainability of what you ship.
 A strong track record of building and operating production software, with substantial ownership of complex systems.
 Experience in data engineering or in building transactional, analytical or distributed systems. You understand the trade-offs behind data models, storage, query execution and service boundaries.
 Experience building products where access control, permissions and data governance are central to how the system works. Work on platforms such as Foundry, or systems with comparable requirements, is particularly relevant.
 Broad software engineering skills and the ability to move between architecture, implementation and production debugging. You are comfortable working across unfamiliar parts of a codebase.
 Strong proficiency in Python or another programming language, solid SQL skills and the ability to become productive quickly in a Python and TypeScript environment.
 High autonomy and sound judgment: you can turn an ambiguous problem into a concrete plan, make technical decisions and deliver useful increments with limited supervision.
 A collaborative approach to technical leadership through code, design discussions, reviews and mentoring, and a clear motivation to build software for defense institutions and industry.
 Nice to have
 Experience building a data platform or developer product used by other engineering teams.
 Experience with fine-grained authorization, multi-tenant architectures, data lineage or auditable operational workflows.
 Experience with self-hosted software, restricted networks or other demanding deployment constraints.
 Familiarity with LLM applications and their integration with data and tools.

items.jobDescription:
About Alta Ares
Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.
 Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
 Founded in 2024, we have grown to 160 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.
 The challenge 
Our operators rely on a ground network that carries telemetry, video and control between drones, antennas and stations, often set up in minutes on unfamiliar terrain. Networking is what turns separate radios, computers and antennas into one system that behaves the same way on every unit. You will configure and debug on the bench, automate deployments, and troubleshoot live links during field trials.
 Missions 
 Design the ground network: addressing, routing, switching and power over Ethernet between stations and antenna systems.
 Integrate telemetry and video flows: MAVLink routing, video streams, latency and reliability measurements.
 Connect the antenna positioning system to the station: control interface, automatic and manual modes.
 Automate provisioning: reference images, router configurations, scripts and checklists so every unit is identical.
 Secure and track deployed systems: workstation hardening, inventory and versions per serial number.
 Required skills 
 Degree in networking, computer or embedded engineering, with experience in network deployment or embedded systems.
 Strong IP networking fundamentals: addressing, VLANs, UDP and multicast, latency and packet-loss diagnostics.
 Tools: Wireshark, router and switch configuration, Windows and Linux, scripting (Python, PowerShell, Bash), Git, Router OS.
 Clear documentation and cybersecurity basics for sensitive environments.
 Autonomous and field-oriented, available for frequent travel.

 Regulated by the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and benefiting from the European passport in 29 countries, Lemonway is based in Paris and brings together 150 multicultural and committed Lemonheroes .

You will actively contribute to delivering our next-generation card payment stack for acquiring and issuing, as well as our cash management platform.
 Your responsibilities
 Technical craftsmanship 
 Deliver features that can evolve, finding the right balance between code quality and delivery time.

 Understand the “why” behind the “what”: bridge the gap between technical implementation and business value, ensuring that our payment flows directly contribute to Lemonway’s operational success and client satisfaction.

 Your qualifications 
 You are curious about emerging engineering tools, including AI-assisted development, and use them thoughtfully to improve productivity, quality, and learning. 
 You have professional experience developing services with modern .NET and C#, and working knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server, RabbitMQ, Docker, and Kubernetes.

 We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents, and disconnected systems.
 Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.
 We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.
 More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling, and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe, and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.
 The Role 
 Legal Solutions Engineers turn the product into real outcomes for customers.
 You’ll work with customers after purchase to design, configure, and implement legal workflows inside Wordsmith. This role sits close to the customer, helping them embed the platform into how their legal function actually operates.
 It’s part implementation, part problem solving, and part advisory. You’ll combine legal understanding with product knowledge to help customers get meaningful value from the platform.
 What you’ll do 
 Customer Implementation 
 Lead implementation projects for new customers
 Design workflows and automation tailored to each organisation
 Configure the platform to support real legal use cases
 Solution Design 
 Work directly with legal teams and Legal Ops leaders to understand how they operate
 Translate legal processes into structured workflows and AI-enabled automation
 Advise on best practices for implementing legal technology
 Customer Success & Expansion 
 Support onboarding and early adoption
 Help customers expand into additional workflows and use cases
 Partner with Account Management to identify growth opportunities
 Product Feedback 
 Surface patterns, insights, and recurring requests to Product and Engineering
 Help shape how the product evolves based on real usage
 What we’re looking for 
 Experience in legal tech, legal operations, or process transformation
 Strong understanding of how in-house legal teams work
 Ability to manage customer projects and guide stakeholders through change
 Comfortable working across legal and technical domains
 Structured thinker — you can turn messy processes into clear systems
 Strong communication skills and confidence working directly with customers
 Typical backgrounds include:
 Legal Engineers
 Legal Operations professionals
 Lawyers who have moved into legal tech
 Implementation or solutions consultants in SaaS with a legal background
 How we work 
 We’re an in-office team in Edinburgh. We work together because it helps us collaborate closely across product, engineering, and customer teams. You should expect to be in the office as your default.
 This is a high ownership role. You’ll be trusted to run projects, work directly with customers, and drive outcomes without heavy oversight.
 The problems are often not fully defined. Part of the role is bringing structure and clarity to how legal work gets done.
 Why this role matters 
 The value of legal technology comes from how it’s implemented.
 Legal Solutions Engineers ensure customers successfully embed Wordsmith into their workflows and see real impact.
 This role sits at the centre of that.
 What you can expect 
 Direct impact on customer outcomes and product adoption

We Are 
 Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 
 You Are 
 You are an experienced implementation engineer with deep expertise across RTL-to-GDSII flows including synthesis, floorplanning, place and route, timing closure, and power optimization. You have worked on complex SoC designs across advanced technology nodes and have a proven track record of improving PPA and driving design closure. You are comfortable working directly with customers, solving challenging implementation issues, running technical evaluations, and demonstrating measurable advantages over competing solutions. You can independently drive engagements, execute benchmarks, and deliver results with minimal supervision. 
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Work with strategic customers to deploy Fusion Compiler on production designs.
 Drive competitive displacement and benchmark engagements by demonstrating superior PPA and productivity results.
 Optimize customer designs across synthesis, place and route, timing, congestion, power, and area.
 Support adoption of new implementation technologies and methodologies.
 Work across a wide range of designs including AI/ML, compute, networking, mobile, and automotive SoCs.
 Collaborate with R&D and product teams to resolve customer issues and influence future product enhancements.
 Provide technical leadership during critical customer milestones and tapeout activities.
 The Impact You Will Have 
 Drive Fusion Compiler adoption at strategic semiconductor accounts.
 Enable competitive wins through benchmark and displacement campaigns.
 Help customers achieve aggressive PPA and schedule targets on advanced-node designs.
 Accelerate deployment of new Synopsys implementation technologies.
 Influence product direction through direct engagement with leading semiconductor companies.
 What You'll Need 
 B.Tech/M.Tech in Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.
 9+ years of experience in ASIC implementation or physical design.
 Strong expertise in RTL-to-GDS flows including synthesis, floorplanning, P&R, CTS, timing closure, and power optimization.
 Experience with advanced-node designs (7nm and below preferred).
 Hands-on experience with Fusion Compiler, Design Compiler, ICC2, or equivalent implementation tools.
 Strong debugging, problem-solving, and customer-facing communication skills.
 Ability to independently drive multiple technical engagements.
 Who You Are 
 You can walk into a customer meeting with a failing timing report, a tight deadline, and incomplete information, and walk out with a clear plan that the customer trusts because you have diagnosed the real problem in the room
 You know the difference between a benchmark that proves a point and one that just generates data, and you structure engagements to answer the question the customer actually cares about, not the one that is easiest to run
 You are technical enough to debug a complex design issue alongside a customer's staff engineer and business-savvy enough to explain the competitive advantage to their director in a way that moves the decision forward
 You do not wait for perfect conditions to deliver results. If the customer's design is messy, the constraints are incomplete, or the timeline is aggressive, you find a way to show progress and build confidence anyway
 You can manage your own pipeline of engagements, prioritize what needs attention today versus next week, and communicate status clearly to internal stakeholders without needing constant check-ins
 You are comfortable being the technical face of Synopsys at a strategic account, which means you take ownership when things go sideways and you follow through until the customer is successful
 The Team You'll Be Part Of 
 The Fusion Compiler Worldwide Engagement Team works with Synopsys' most strategic customers to drive new technology adoption, execute competitive displacement campaigns, and deliver industry-leading PPA results. The team works across diverse design styles, applications, and technology nodes, partnering closely with R&D and field teams to accelerate customer success and business growth. 
 Rewards and Benefits 
 We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process. 
 At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

We are a multidisciplinary, hands-on group of product integration, optics, hardware, and firmware engineers who work closely with global partner teams while maintaining end-to-end local ownership in our Nuremberg laboratories.  Your Impact
 As a Product Integration & Firmware Development Engineer , you will operate at the critical intersection of hands-on electro-optic lab bring-up and embedded software development.  Architect & Develop Embedded Firmware: Design, implement, and maintain high-reliability embedded firmware in C (and C++) for microcontroller- and ASIC-based controllers within optical modules.
 Implement Device Diagnostics & Control: Develop low-level device control, system monitoring, diagnostic routines, fault handling, and management interfaces compliant with CMIS (Common Management Interface Specification) and applicable SFF standards.

 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.
 Hands-on proficiency with low-level communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, MDIO), reading schematics and component datasheets, and using embedded lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG).
 Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, lead technical problem-solving investigations, and summarize and present complex project details clearly to cross-functional teams.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience developing firmware with a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) in resource-constrained environments.
 Domain knowledge of optical transceivers (100G+ per lane), coherent optics, high-speed SerDes, DSPs, or optical monitoring subsystems.
 In-depth understanding of optical management and communications standards, such as CMIS (Common Management Interface Specification), SFF specifications, and Ethernet protocols.
 Proficiency in Python or similar scripting languages for test automation, lab instrumentation control, and systematic data analysis.
 Background in Design Verification Testing (DVT), product qualification lifecycles, or manufacturing test

 Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Technology adoption.

 The Agentic Work Environment team 
 The Agentic Work Environment (AWE) owns the environment everyone at Multiverse works in, wherever they are in the world. That covers the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day, the platform our product is built and run on, and the identity and access that decide who, or which agent, can do what across all of it. Product teams own what they build; we own the ground it stands on, the path it takes to production, and the baseline standards it meets on the way. Our mission is to make the safe way the fast way for every colleague and the agents they put to work.
 For a security-minded AI engineer, that remit runs in two directions. In the product platform, you build security into the path itself: review agents that check every change against our baseline standards, one identity for customers, staff and agents, and detection and response through our SIEM and SOAR, so nobody, person or agent, has to remember to be secure. In the workplace, you secure the devices, tools and accounts colleagues around the world rely on.  What your day-to-day will look like

 Build security into the path to production. Staying on the path should meet the security requirements without any extra work.
 Secure the agents we and our colleagues build. You threat-model agent systems end to end, from prompt injection and tool misuse to data leaking through context and retrieval, and design the controls that stop it: scoped tool permissions, permission-aware retrieval, sandboxing, and human approval where the risk calls for it.
 Give every agent an identity. You build the identity and access layer for agents. Each one has its own identity, a named owner, least-privilege access that is reviewed and can be revoked at once, and a full record of what it did.
 Build detection and response with agents. You write detections and automated responses on our SIEM and SOAR, and build agents that triage alerts, gather context and carry out bounded, reversible responses, so people spend their time on the cases that need judgement.
 Secure the workplace, worldwide. You apply the same approach to the devices, workplace tools and accounts colleagues use every day: automated controls rather than manual checklists, and access that is granted and removed as people join, move and leave.
 Prove it holds with security evals. You build eval pipelines and red-team exercises that show whether our agents and controls stand up to attack, and produce compliance evidence as a by-product of the work rather than as screenshots for an auditor.
 Influence technical direction. You have opinions about how things should be built, and you back them up with evidence. You contribute to architectural decisions, push back when the team is heading in the wrong direction, and propose better approaches.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Entwicklungsteams am Standort Haan suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt einen Embedded Software / Firmware Engineer (m/w/d) .
In dieser Rolle übernehmen Sie eine zentrale Funktion bei der Entwicklung und Optimierung unserer analytischen Messgeräte und arbeiten eng mit interdisziplinären Teams aus Elektronik, Mechanik, Anwendungstechnik zusammen.
Ihre Aufgaben als Embedded Software / Firmware Engineer (m/w/d) – ELTRA:
 Entwicklung, Implementierung und Pflege von Firmware für Embedded Systeme und Mikrocontroller-basierte Messgeräte.
 Umsetzung von Signalverarbeitung und Datenaufbereitung direkt in der Firmware.
 Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Hardwareentwicklung, Mechanik und Anwendungstechnik zur Definition von Anforderungen und Schnittstellen.
 Analyse, Debugging und Optimierung von Software hinsichtlich Performance, Stabilität und Ressourceneffizienz.
 Planung und Durchführung von Modul-, Integrations- und Systemtests zur Sicherstellung der Softwarequalität.
 Erstellung und Pflege technischer Dokumentationen (Design, Implementierung, Tests).
 Begleitung des gesamten Entwicklungsprozesses – von der Konzeptphase über Prototypen bis hin zur Inbetriebnahme der Geräte am Standort Haan.
 Ihr Profil als Embedded Software / Firmware Engineer (m/w/d) – ELTRA:
 Abgeschlossenes Studium oder Technikerabschluss in Elektrotechnik, Informatik, Mechatronik oder Automatisierungstechnik (oder vergleichbar).
 Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Embedded Software- bzw. Firmware-Entwicklung, idealerweise im Geräte- oder Maschinenumfeld und solide Kenntnisse in Altium.
 Sehr gute Kenntnisse in C/C++, SPI, I2C, AN, Ethernet, PIC32, PI5
 Erfahrung mit KI-gestützter Softwareentwicklung von Vorteil.
 Erfahrung mit hardwarenaher Programmierung, Mikrocontrollern sowie idealerweise RTOS oder Embedded Linux.
 Verständnis für Signalverarbeitung sowie Erfahrung im Umgang mit Mess- oder Analysesystemen von Vorteil.
 Erfahrung mit Versionsverwaltung (z. B. Git) sowie strukturierten Entwicklungsprozessen.
 Analytische Denkweise, strukturierte Arbeitsweise sowie ausgeprägte Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit.

 We're looking for a Senior AI Automation & Systems Engineer to own the technical infrastructure behind our content and design operation, from planning and research, through AI-assisted production and quality control, to publishing and distribution.

 Take technical ownership of our content and design factory: tooling selection, automation pipelines, quality management, and agent orchestration that let a small team produce at scale.

 Competitive salary and room to grow as our ambitions scale.

Founded in 2000, the firm has offices in London, New York, Hong Kong and Abu Dhabi, and currently manages $9 billion in assets across five funds.  Job description: 
 We are seeking a DevOps Engineer to join our technology team in London. This role helps build and maintain the infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and monitoring that our trading, research, and operations systems run on. It is a hands-on position with a broad remit, offering real ownership and visible impact on how the business runs.
 The role sits alongside software developers, data engineers, and infrastructure staff, with support from senior engineers as the successful candidate develops. We are looking for someone curious and methodical, who enjoys understanding how systems fit together and takes pride in making things reliable and repeatable rather than merely working.

 Build, maintain, and improve CI/CD pipelines for internal applications, working with developers to make releases faster, safer, and more automated.
 Support day-to-day requests from development teams, helping developers debug build, deployment and environment issues.
 Support and extend our cloud and on-premise infrastructure, including provisioning environments and managing configuration through infrastructure-as-code.
 Help operate monitoring, alerting, and logging so that issues are caught before they affect users, and contribute to investigating and resolving incidents when they occur.
 Write scripts and small tools to automate manual and repetitive operational tasks.
 Contribute to improving software delivery practices across the technology team.
 Participate in an on-call rotation, providing out of hours support for DevOps related issues impacting critical services.
 Required qualities and skills: 
 3+ years of experience in a DevOps, platform, infrastructure, or software engineering role, including internships and placements.
 Experience with Git and standard branching and code review workflows.
 Experience with CI/CD tooling, particularly GitHub Actions.
 Exposure to containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, etc).
 Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools, particularly Terraform.
 Experience working with a major cloud platform (Azure, GCP, AWS).
 Understanding of networking fundamentals (DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP, load balancing, firewalls).
 Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical issues to colleagues from non-technical teams.
 Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell, or Bash.
 Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a closely related field, or equivalent experience.
 Preferred: 
 Working knowledge of Linux and/or Windows Server administration.

Wie ontwerpt het fundament waarop soevereine cloudplatformen kunnen bouwen? 
 Iedere organisatie die naar schaalbare, soevereine Cloudinfrastructuur beweegt, botst vroeg of laat op dezelfde vraag: wie zorgt dat die infrastructuur betrouwbaar, reproduceerbaar en toekomstbestendig is, zonder in te leveren op controle en portabiliteit? Als Platform Engineer is dat jouw vraagstuk.
 De uitdaging 
 Als Platform Engineer kom je in dienst bij LINKIT en ga je aan het werk bij toonaangevende opdrachtgevers zoals Defensie, KLM en ASML, aan complexe infrastructuurvraagstukken op seniorniveau. Je ontwerpt, bouwt en beheert Cloudinfrastructuur en CI/CD-pipelines, geeft vorm aan platformarchitecturen, zoals het deployen van Mendix op Kubernetes-clusters binnen Europese cloudomgevingen, en zet Kubernetes-clusters op binnen Europese Cloudproviders als STACKIT, OVH en Scaleway of binnen private Cloudomgevingen. Met Infrastructure as Code, bijvoorbeeld Terraform, maak je infrastructuren reproduceerbaar en schaalbaar. Je werkt nauw samen met software-, data- en AI-engineers, en met klanten om infrastructuurbehoeften te vertalen naar betrouwbare oplossingen, met oog voor soevereiniteit, autonomie en portabiliteit.
 Je plek: de Platform Engineering squad 
 Je landt in de Platform Engineering squad, waar collega's elkaar scherp houden op technische keuzes en architectuur. Om de twee weken kom je op vrijdag terug naar ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern voor de clubdag, waarop we tijd vrijmaken voor kennisdeling, leren en verbinden met de rest van LINKIT.
 Lees  hier  meer over de Platform Engineering squad. 
 Wat we vragen 
 Minimaal 4 jaar ervaring in een DevOps-, Platform Engineering- of infrastructuurrol, bij voorkeur binnen de Nederlandse overheid.
 Aantoonbare ervaring met containers en orchestratieplatformen zoals Kubernetes en Docker, gecombineerd met CI/CD-tooling zoals GitHub Actions, GitLab CI of Jenkins, en Infrastructure as Code, bijvoorbeeld Terraform.
 Ervaring met cloud-agnostisch werken binnen publieke en private cloudomgevingen, waaronder Europese providers als STACKIT, OVH en Scaleway en platformen zoals OpenStack.
 Ervaring met automatisering en scripting, met tools en talen zoals Python, Go, Ansible en/of Chef.
 Kennis van netwerken, beveiliging en observability binnen cloud-native en on-premise omgevingen.
 Affiniteit met open-source tooling en moderne data-infrastructuren, zoals datapipelines, datawarehouses, lakehouses en MLOps.
 Voldoe je niet aan elk punt, maar wel nieuwsgierig? Dan komen we alsnog graag met je in contact.
 Wat je krijgt 
 Salaris tussen €4.300-€6.700 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur, afhankelijk van kennis & ervaring) + 8% vakantiegeld.
 Jaarlijkse winstdeling en pensioenregeling.
 Hybride werken: op ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern, bij de klant of vanuit huis.
 25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om tijdelijk vanuit het buitenland te werken.
 Elektrische leaseauto of mobiliteitsvergoeding.
 Netto thuiswerkvergoeding, een goed ingerichte thuiswerkplek en een laptop + telefoon, die je ook privé kunt gebruiken.
 Om de twee weken op vrijdag komen alle collega's terug naar ons hoofdkantoor in De Meern, dan investeren wij tot 10% van jouw werktijd in kennisdeling, leren en verbinden (dit noemen wij de 'clubdag').
 Extra's zoals onbeperkt opleidingsbudget, dagelijkse verse lunch, jaarlijks wintersport en wellbeing-activiteiten, , zoals een wijnproeverij en yoga.
 Sollicitatieprocedure 
 We willen je leren kennen, en jij ons. Daarom houden we het persoonlijk en concreet.
 Kennismaking: een eerste gesprek over wie je bent, wat je drijft en of er een match is.
 Verdiepende gesprekken: twee gesprekken over je ervaring, werkwijze en hoe jij past binnen de squad en bij onze klanten.
 Aanbieding: als het klikt, volgt een concreet aanbod.
 Wil je alvast meer weten? Neem gerust contact op met Tabea via 
 Over LINKIT 
 LINKIT is opgericht in 1998 en gegroeid van IT-bemiddelaar naar kennisgedreven IT-organisatie, met ruim 250 Explorers uit meer dan 25 nationaliteiten. We werken voor grote organisaties in overheid, finance en logistiek als partner die meedenkt van vraagstuk tot oplossing. Als Platform Engineer ga je aan het werk bij toonaangevende opdrachtgevers, met een contract bij LINKIT. Je bepaalt je eigen richting, met een ongelimiteerd opleidingsbudget en de ruimte om te groeien op een manier die bij jou past.

 Lead the evolution of CI/CD pipelines and GitOps-based workflows.
 Build and maintain internal platform services and tooling that improve developer experience and delivery velocity
 Continue to drive Infrastructure as Code and automation practices across teams
 Partner with application teams to unblock delivery and align platform capabilities with developer needs
 Participate in and/or lead complex, cross-team initiatives and provide technical clarity in ambiguous problem spaces
 Improve operational excellence through observability, automation, and incident response.
 Mentor engineers and participate in on-call rotations
 What You Bring 
 8+ years of experience in platform, infrastructure, DevOps, or software engineering
 Proficiency with Python and Java. Familiarity with Kotlin, Go a plus
 Deep Kubernetes and container orchestration knowledge
 Proven CI/CD and GitOps experience
 Infrastructure as Code expertise (Terraform)
 Strong AWS and cloud-native experience
 Experience operating distributed, high-availability systems
 Ability to influence without authority and communicate effectively across regions
 Nice to Have 
 Experience with internal developer platforms or portals
 FinOps or cloud cost management experience
 Regulated or high-availability environment experience
 Backend development experience
 Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools
 Why Platform Engineering at FBG 
 Platform Engineering at FBG operates with a product-first mindset. Our mission is to empower developers with reliable, scalable, and intuitive platforms that accelerate innovation and delivery.
 Working Across Regions 
 This role operates in a globally distributed environment, working closely with teams across the UK, Ireland, and the United States. Strong communication, time zone coordination, and shared ownership are essential for success.

Vorweg, damit wir uns die Zeit sparen: Diese Rolle ist neu bei uns. Du verbindest Beratung, Technik und Prototyping – und bist dabei schneller als jede Folie.
 Wenn ein Kunde im Workshop sagt „Unsere Produktdaten sind ein Chaos“, willst du kein Konzept schreiben, das in drei Wochen fertig ist. Du willst ihm am Nachmittag zeigen, wie es aussehen könnte.
 Wenn du bei „Workshop“ an Moderationskarten und Flipchart denkst, wird das hier nichts. Wenn du dabei an deinen Laptop mit Claude Code denkst: lies weiter.
 Wer wir sind 
 creativestyle ist eine E-Commerce-Agentur mit deutsch-polnischem Setup: Beratung und Projektmanagement in München, Entwicklung in Krakau und Rybnik. Über 120 umgesetzte Shops, rund 110 Leute, Kunden wie NKD, Mövenpick, CEWE Fotobuch, Einhell und Bergzeit.
 Dieses Jahr haben wir richtig abgeräumt: Agentur des Jahres , dazu zwei Auszeichnungen gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden – Best Customer Experience mit benuta, Best Mobile Experience mit Bergzeit.
 Was das im Alltag bedeutet:
 Jede und jeder bei uns hat einen technischen Background. Die Geschäftsführung eingeschlossen.
 50 % Freiheit, 50 % Verantwortung. Beides gilt gleichzeitig.
 Fehler sind bei uns Lektionen, keine Schuldfrage. Wir steigen nur ungern zweimal in denselben Fluss.
 Corporate sind wir nicht. Unzuverlässig allerdings auch nicht.
 Wir nehmen keine Projekte an, auf die wir keine Lust haben.
 Warum wir diese Stelle gerade jetzt schaffen 
 Zwei Gründe, beide ehrlich:
 1. Unsere Kunden wollen keine Shops mehr. Sie wollen Lösungen. Produktdaten, ERP, Schnittstellen, Automatisierung, KI – die spannenden Fragen liegen heute zwischen den Systemen. Dafür brauchen wir Leute, die im Workshop zuhören, verstehen, wo es wirklich weh tut, und einen Vorschlag auf den Tisch legen, den man anfassen kann.
 2. KI verändert, wie Beratung funktioniert. Ein Prototyp dauert heute Stunden statt Wochen. Wir wollen Kunden nicht erklären, was möglich wäre – wir wollen es ihnen zeigen. Du bist die erste Person in dieser Rolle und gestaltest sie von Anfang an mit.
 Deine Mission 
 Verstehen, bevor du löst. Du führst Discovery-Workshops mit unseren Kunden: Prozesse, Datenflüsse, Systemlandschaft. Du fragst so lange nach, bis klar ist, wo das eigentliche Problem liegt – und das steht selten im Briefing.
 Nie mit leeren Händen kommen. Vor dem Workshop baust du eine erste Version. Im Workshop diskutiert ihr am konkreten Beispiel statt an abstrakten Folien. Manchmal iterierst du live, während alle zuschauen.
 Vibe-Coding als Werkzeug, nicht als Spielerei. Vor allem mit Claude Code baust du in Stunden einen klickbaren Prototyp: ein PIM-Datenmodell, einen Schnittstellen-Mock, einen KI-Agenten, der Produkttexte schreibt. Produktionscode schreiben unsere Devs in Polen. Dein Job ist zu zeigen, was möglich ist.
 Lösungen skizzieren, die halten. Shop, PIM, ERP, KI – du zeichnest, wer was macht, wo die Daten leben und wie die Systeme miteinander reden. Und du kannst begründen, warum.
 Die Brücke ins Team. Nach dem Workshop übergibst du an Projektleitung und Entwicklung so, dass alle wissen, was gebaut wird und warum. Bei Pitches bist du dabei, wenn es technisch konkret wird.
 Du bist unser Mensch, wenn 
 Du verstehst, wie ein Händler tickt: Produktdaten, Bestellungen, Bestände, Kanäle. Ob du aus Beratung, Pre-Sales, Projektleitung oder Entwicklung kommst, ist uns egal.
 Du technisch wirklich mitreden kannst: Datenmodelle, APIs, Schnittstellen, Systemarchitektur. Produktionscode musst du nicht schreiben. Aber du kannst erklären, warum eine Variante kein eigenes Produkt ist und wann ein Webhook besser ist als der nächtliche CSV-Export.
 KI-Tools dein Alltag sind, nicht dein Vorsatz fürs nächste Jahr. Du hast damit schon Dinge gebaut, die funktionieren – und zeigst sie uns gern.
 Du einen Raum führen kannst: acht Leute aus Einkauf, IT und Marketing, drei Meinungen pro Person, und am Ende trotzdem ein Ergebnis.
 Du Fragen stellst, bevor du Antworten gibst.
 Es dich nicht nervös macht, Unfertiges zu zeigen. Ein Prototyp ist zum Kaputtmachen da.
 Du fließend Deutsch (C2) und sehr gut Englisch sprichst – unsere Kunden sitzen im DACH-Raum, unsere Teams in Polen.
 Pluspunkte sammelst du mit Shopware, Magento oder Shopify, mit PIM- oder ERP-Erfahrung (Pimcore, Akeneo, Odoo, SAP, Business Central) und mit Erfahrung auf Händlerseite.
 Wir bauen ein offenes Team. Bewirb dich unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Herkunft, Orientierung, Religion oder Behinderung – uns interessiert, was du kannst und wie du denkst.
 Was du bei uns bekommst 
 Gehalt: abhängig von deiner Erfahrung. Konkrete Zahlen gibt es beim ersten Gespräch, nicht erst nach der dritten Runde.
 Innovationsbudget für PoCs und eigene Ideen – bewusst als Investment gedacht, nicht als Restposten.
 Weiterbildungsbudget inklusive Zertifizierungen.
 Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Home Office. Die Arbeit passt sich deinem Leben an, nicht umgekehrt.
 Büro mit Dachterrasse im TRI München – plus MVV-Ticket, damit du auch hinkommst.
 MacBook Pro und iPhone , ordentliche Peripherie inklusive.
 Teamevents in Deutschland und Polen. Epische Trips nach Polen und die legendäre Revanche der polnischen Crew auf der Wiesn.
 Kaffee, Getränke und Obst. Muss man ja heute dazuschreiben.
 Klingt nach dir? 
 Dann bewirb dich über unser Bewerbungsformular oder schick deine Unterlagen an ----- Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Viel lieber: ein Link zu etwas, das du mit KI gebaut hast. Darf ruhig unfertig sein.
 Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Du findest Fehler nicht nur – du sorgst dafür, dass sie gar nicht erst entstehen.

 Als Test Engineer / Test Automation Engineer übernimmst du Verantwortung für die Qualitätssicherung moderner Softwarelösungen.  Du erstellst, dokumentierst und führst manuelle sowie automatisierte Softwaretests durch.
 Du planst und realisierst Integrations- und Regressionstests für unterschiedliche Softwarelösungen.

At Studytube, we're not just another EdTech company from Amsterdam. We've taken on a big challenge: helping organisations close the skills gap and giving employees the room to grow. Our platform shows companies which skills really matter, where the biggest gaps are, and how to tackle them. But real impact takes more than a strong product — it comes from creating relevant experiences, sharp storytelling, and engagement that actually means something.
 That’s why we’re looking for a Solutions Engineer who bridges commercial ambition and technical-legal reality. You secure the ‘Technical Win’ in complex sales trajectories and enterprise tenders, acting as trusted advisor so every proposal is commercially winning, technically defensible and fully aligned with client needs and regulatory standards. 
 What you will do 
 As Solutions Engineer you own the engineering and advisory layer that turns complex customer requirements into robust, secure solutions across the full sales cycle. You are building the so-called “technical/product champion” alongside the AE in the sales process. Activities that come along with winning customers from the solution engineering perspective are: 
 You design and configure platform solutions for complex enterprise scenarios, including deep integrations, custom roles, automations and external content sources, so every demo and proposal is tailored and technically sound. 
 You analyse RFPs/RFIs and PvE documents, identify gaps, manage the Memorandum of Information (NVI/Q&A) process and craft high-quality qualitative narratives on topics such as security, architecture, accessibility and continuity. 
 You lead technical deep-dives, workshops and on-site UAT sessions, remove blockers in real time and build consensus with IT stakeholders, CISOs and C-level decision makers. 
 You map client IT landscapes, design complex integrations (SSO, AFAS, SAP, Learning Hub/DMS and others) and visualise data flows in professional architecture diagrams. 
 You navigate and translate security & privacy frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, BIO, DORA, Archives Act) into concrete product proof-points and commercial advantages. 
 You act as the bridge between Sales, Engineering, Product and Compliance — harvesting tribal knowledge, feeding market insights back into the roadmap and turning technical complexity into reusable commercial assets. 
 You use AI tools as your daily operating system: analysing lengthy RFPs, generating first-draft responses, accelerating narrative writing and building custom assistants while keeping human-in-the-loop quality and security standards. 
 You measure success by technical wins secured, sales cycles de-risked, time saved for the commercial team and long-term institutional trust built with enterprise clients — not just documents delivered. 
 Who you are 
 You have 3 to 7 years of experience in Solutions Engineering, Pre-Sales, Technical Consulting or a similar role at a scaling B2B SaaS company, preferably EdTech or tech. You’ve moved beyond standard demos into complex enterprise solution design and tender support. 
 You have hands-on experience configuring platforms, scoping integrations, working with APIs and data models, and shipping working technical answers under tender deadlines. 
 You’re fluent in both the commercial conversation (with Account Executives and SDRs) and the technical conversation (with architects, CISOs and engineers). 
 You’re AI-native and product-minded: you diagnose requirements, design solutions, ship documentation and iterate with commercial outcomes in mind. AI is your building material. 
 You’re structured, detail-oriented, proactive and able to keep overview across multiple parallel tenders and stakeholder groups. 
 You think commercially — about which technical choices increase win probability, reduce risk and create long-term trust, not just technical elegance. 
 You’re a strong team player with excellent communication skills and the ability to make complex topics accessible and exciting. 
 You speak and write excellent Dutch (English is a plus). 
 What we offer 
 €60K - €80K a year including holiday allowence + 10K variabel. 
 Flexible working hours. 
 Hybrid working (3 days at the office / 2 days at home). 
 25 holidays + an extra day off on your birthday. 
 A 3% pension contribution paid by Studytube via A.S.R. 
 A fully equipped gym at the office — work out before or after work and skip the trip to Basic-Fit. 
 €1,000 L&D budget per year, of which 50% can go towards wellbeing or your home-office setup. 
 In-company training via our own Studytube Academy: LevelUp. 
 A beautiful office in the Houthavens with a view over the IJ. 
 A company laptop (MacBook Air) + €10 allowance for using your own phone. 
 For a small contribution: a fully catered lunch with a choice of a hot meal, sandwiches or salad bar when you’re at the office. 
 The nicest colleagues, with a team outing every quarter and an annual company party. 
 About Studytube 
Studytube makes professional development as accessible, easy, fun, and successful as possible. We believe it’s essential for companies to invest in employee development, now more than ever. That’s why we offer an all-in-one learning platform that inspires employees to grow—and we do so successfully. Our customer portfolio includes over 300 clients across various industries, ranging from 200 to 30,000 employees. Companies like Bol.com, ASR, CZ, Manpower, VolkerWessels, and Eneco are already inspiring their employees with our platform. Together with 200+ diverse and passionate colleagues, we focus on creating the best learning experience for our clients. Our goal? To become Europe’s #1 platform for professional development.

Role Highlights
 Role: Forward Deployed AI Engineer
 Department: Forward Deployed Engineering
 Location: Germany 
 Reports to: VP, Forward Deployed Engineering
 Working type: Hybrid (On-site at customer locations approx. 50% of time)
 German security clearance (Sicherheitsüberprüfung Ü1/Ü2/Ü3)
 Must be eligible and able to attain relevant national and NATO security clearances
 Must be based in-country and native level speaker of the country you're deploying to. 
 The Mission of the Forward Deployed AI Engineer
 In this role, you'll be the hands-on AI builder defense and intelligence customers rely on. You’ll deploy ICEYE’s intelligence platform into secure (often air-gapped) environments and rapidly ship AI-powered workflows on top of it—everything from Docker-based deployments to RAG systems fusing SAR imagery with intelligence reports. This is a ship-code-daily role: turning raw satellite data into mission-critical tools analysts use to protect nations.
 Who We Are
 ICEYE is the world leader in sovereign intelligence from space. We deliver persistent monitoring capabilities to detect and respond to changes in any location on Earth.
ICEYE owns the world's largest and most advanced SAR (synthetic aperture radar) satellite constellation. To our customers we provide intelligence with unmatched quality, latency and revisit times, in any weather, day or night. To governments who choose to operate their own constellation we provide this proven capability as a sovereign system.
ICEYE-built constellations serve customers in defence and intelligence, environmental monitoring, insurance and emergency management. We enable fast decisions that contribute to a safer future.
Founded and headquartered in Finland, ICEYE operates globally with over 1000 employees across Europe, North America, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.
 Day To Day Responsibilities
 Platform Deployment & Integration
 Deploy ICEYE's intelligence platform into customer secure environments (on-premise, air-gapped networks, classified data centers).
 Build and maintain containerized applications (Docker) and manage deployments in customer Kubernetes clusters.
 Develop APIs and data pipelines connecting ICEYE systems to customer C4ISR infrastructure and intelligence tools.
 Troubleshoot deployment issues in disconnected environments without external internet access.
 AI Solution Development & Customization
 Build Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems that combine ICEYE SAR data with customer intelligence documents for context-aware analysis.
 Develop AI agents and workflows using frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, or similar tools to automate analytical tasks.
 Implement prompt engineering strategies and conversational AI interfaces that enable analysts to query satellite data using natural language.
 Create Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations connecting AI systems with customer data sources.
 Data Fusion & Intelligence Workflows
 Build data fusion pipelines combining SAR imagery with additional intelligence sources (AIS, RF signals, optical imagery, SIGINT).
 Develop automated workflows that correlate and cross-reference information across different data modalities.
 Create lightweight tools, dashboards, and alerting systems tailored to customer operational needs.
 Customer Engagement & Rapid Prototyping
 Work embedded with intelligence analysts, data scientists, and military operators to understand mission-critical problems.
 Rapidly prototype AI-powered solutions (code first, polish later) that address immediate operational requirements.
 Conduct hands-on training sessions on platform capabilities and AI workflow usage.
 Gather customer feedback and translate it into technical requirements for ICEYE's product and engineering teams.
 What we are looking for
 Must Have Skills
 3+ years hands-on software engineering building and deploying production systems.
 Strong Python programming skills (required) plus one of: Go, TypeScript, or Rust.
 Hands-on experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, and RAG systems.
 Working knowledge of agent frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, pydantic-ai) and vector databases.
 Experience with Docker and deploying in secure / isolated / air-gapped environments.
 Practical experience with APIs, data pipelines, and integrating systems in production,
 Familiarity with Linux and basic Kubernetes operations.
 Builder mindset: ship fast, iterate with feedback, and prioritize working solutions over perfect architecture.
 Strong communication + customer engagement, able to work embedded with intelligence analysts / military operators.
 Strong spoken and written English, able to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
 Willingness to travel 40–60% to customer sites within the region.
 Nice To Have Skills
 Experience in defense, intelligence, or government operational environments.
 Deploying to on-prem data centers and/or air-gapped networks.
 Familiarity with geospatial data, satellite imagery, or remote sensing.
 Experience with MCP integrations, multi-agent systems, or agentic workflows.
 Deeper Kubernetes, IaC (Terraform/Ansible), and/or offline CI/CD.
 Understanding of intelligence analysis workflows and defense/government requirements.
 Experience with data fusion, multi-source intelligence integration, or GIS tools (ArcGIS, QGIS).
 Background in solution engineering, technical consulting, or customer success.
 Experience in defense tech (e.g., Palantir, Anduril, Scale AI, similar startups).
 Application process
 Talent Acquisition Interview
 Take home task
 Hiring Manager Interview
 Hiring Team Interview
 Offer Decision
 Working at ICEYE
 At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.
 How We Work (Our Values)
 Make the impossible possible: We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.
 Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.
 See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.
 Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.
 Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.
 Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.
 Benefits
 Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing—at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.
 Our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
 We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.
We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.
Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com

 Contribute to networked air defense: Help integrate our systems into multi-layered defense architectures alongside sensors, command systems, and effectors
